title: Apple’s market value drops below $2 trillion
summary: Apple Inc.'s market capitalization fell below $2 trillion for the first time since March 2021, driven by concerns over high inflation and a slowing global economy impacting demand for its products. This significant drop follows a year after the company briefly reached a $3 trillion valuation. Analysts have downgraded Apple due to anticipated supply chain issues and reduced consumer spending on high-end phones, forecasting a potential revenue decline.

title: HDFC Bank partners with Microsoft to drive its digital transformation efforts
summary: HDFC Bank has partnered with Microsoft to accelerate its digital transformation agenda, focusing on modernizing its data landscape, application portfolio, and enhancing enterprise security. The collaboration will leverage Microsoft's Azure cloud platform for a Federated Data Lake, enabling data monetization and democratizing access across business units. Additionally, HDFC Bank will utilize Microsoft Power Platform for app innovation and automation, and Microsoft 365 for a secure and collaborative digital workplace.

title: HDFC Bank partners with Microsoft as part of its digital transformation journey
summary: HDFC Bank is partnering with Microsoft to accelerate its digital transformation, focusing on modernizing its data landscape, enhancing employee productivity, and securing its enterprise with Microsoft Cloud. The collaboration involves leveraging Microsoft Azure for a Federated Data Lake, using Microsoft Power Platform to build an App Innovation and Automation Factory, and deploying Microsoft 365 and Security solutions to achieve a secure and integrated digital workplace. This initiative aims to provide a superior neo-banking experience for customers and support the bank's "Future Ready" strategy.

title: Pulp and Paper Industry 2022 Year in Review
summary: The pulp and paper industry in 2022 was heavily impacted by widespread supply chain disruptions, including a four-month strike at UPM's Finnish mills and the Russian invasion of Ukraine, which led to sanctions and an energy crisis. Despite these challenges, major grades like containerboard and tissue and towel showed significant growth, driven by e-commerce and increasing demand, respectively. The year also saw notable project progress, such as Klabin's Puma II project for Eukaliner production, and a wave of strategic divestitures, acquisitions, and mergers across Europe, North America, and Latin America.

title: A bird’s eye view of Data Centers
summary: Uma Iyer's article offers a comprehensive overview of India's data center landscape, highlighting the rapid growth spurred by data booms, digital adoption, and local data storage mandates. It details the top 15 data center providers in India, their current capacities, expansion plans, and commitments to sustainability, while also forecasting a future shift towards Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities due to high costs in major metropolitan areas.

title: CES: Intel Extends Performance Leadership with World's Fastest Mobile Processor
summary: At CES 2023, Intel launched its 13th Gen Intel Core mobile processor family, including the flagship Intel Core i9-13980HX, dubbed the world's fastest mobile processor and the first 24-core processor for a laptop. Intel also introduced new 13th Gen Intel Core desktop processors and the Intel Processor N-series for education and entry-level computing. These advancements aim to deliver superior performance, better battery life, and enhanced experiences across various computing segments, from enthusiast gaming laptops to thin-and-light devices and IoT applications.

title: Amazon's AWS Growth Strategy Probably More Sustainable Than Oracle's (AMZN)
summary: The article compares the sustainability of growth strategies between Amazon's AWS and Oracle. While Oracle has seen growth due to acquisitions and price cutting, AWS's growth is attributed to its vertically integrated cloud infrastructure and product strength, accounting for a significant portion of Amazon's profits. The author suggests Oracle's strategy may not be sustainable given its debt-to-sales ratio and profitability, and advises that Oracle needs a clearer plan for profitable growth.

title: AMD Highlights Future of High-Performance and Adaptive Computing During Opening Keynote of CES 2023
summary: During the CES 2023 opening keynote, AMD Chair and CEO Dr. Lisa Su showcased new leadership products across various markets, emphasizing the role of high-performance and adaptive computing in solving global challenges. AMD unveiled new mobile and desktop processors, including the first x86 PC CPU with a dedicated AI engine and desktop processors with 3D V-Cache technology, alongside new graphics solutions. The company also previewed advancements in AI with the Alveo V70 AI Accelerator and Instinct MI300, and highlighted the use of AMD technology in healthcare and aerospace.

title: Salesforce to cut 10% of workforce in latest tech layoffs
summary: Salesforce Inc. announced it will cut 10% of its workforce and close some offices, aiming to reduce costs after rapid hiring during the pandemic. Co-CEO Marc Benioff stated the company hired "too many people" leading into the current economic downturn, taking responsibility for the over-hiring. This move follows similar workforce reductions by other tech giants like Meta and Amazon, as companies prepare for a potential deep downturn amid rising interest rates and a challenging economic environment.

title: Distributed Cloud Global Market Report 2022: Ukraine-Russia War Impact
summary: The global distributed cloud market is projected to grow significantly, from $2.84 billion in 2021 to $7.42 billion in 2026, despite disruptions caused by the Russia-Ukraine war and the COVID-19 pandemic. This growth is driven by the increasing adoption of distributed cloud architectures to meet performance, compliance, and edge computing demands. Technological innovation, such as F5's Distributed Cloud WAAP, is a key trend, with companies focusing on advanced solutions to secure and manage applications across multi-cloud environments.

title: HP launches PCs for hybrid workers with 'world-first' dual-camera setups
summary: HP unveiled new PCs at CES 2023, specifically designed for hybrid workers, featuring what it calls a 'world-first' dual-camera setup that allows for simultaneous video streams and camera switching. These devices, including the HP Dragonfly G4, HP EliteBook 1040 G10, and HP Elite x360 1040 G10, are equipped with Intel 13th Gen processors and aim to enhance productivity and connectivity in flexible work environments. Additionally, HP introduced the Dragonfly Pro Chromebook and HP Dragonfly Pro targeted at users needing continuous connectivity, powerful cameras, and dedicated support for demanding workloads, appealing to the growing freelance community.

title: The Power of 7: Tech that will disrupt 2023
summary: This article identifies seven key technology trends poised for significant disruption in 2023. These include advancements in Unsupervised Machine Learning, Robotic Process Automation, expanded applications of Virtual and Augmented Reality, the increasing sophistication of AI Chatbots, widespread adoption of 5G, the growth of the Internet of Things, and the emergence of AI-driven programming. The author highlights how these innovations will impact various industries, from healthcare and e-commerce to manufacturing, and discusses their potential effects on global GDP and job markets.

title: PurpleUrchin Bypasses CAPTCHA and Steals Cloud Platform Resources
summary: Unit 42 researchers at Palo Alto Networks have identified a "freejacking" campaign called PurpleUrchin, orchestrated by the threat actor group Automated Libra. This group exploits free or limited-time cloud resources, leveraging DevOps automation and CAPTCHA bypass techniques to conduct cryptocurrency mining operations. They also employ a "Play and Run" tactic, creating fake accounts with fraudulent credit card information to incur unpaid balances on cloud service platforms, having created over 130,000 such accounts.

title: Warning over ransomware attacks spreading via Fortinet kit
summary: Ransomware operators are exploiting a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2022-40684) in Fortinet VPN devices, which was disclosed in October 2022. eSentire's Threat Research Unit has observed threat actors scanning for vulnerable devices and successfully exploiting them in two attacks against customers, with access to compromised devices also being sold on the dark web. The security firm emphasizes the risks posed by misconfigured and third-party managed SSL VPNs, highlighting the need for vigilant monitoring and endpoint security solutions.

title: Comcast Promotes Jason S. Armstrong to CFO
summary: Comcast has appointed Jason S. Armstrong as its new Chief Financial Officer. Armstrong, who previously served as deputy CFO and treasurer, steps into the role formerly held by Mike Cavanagh, who was promoted to company president in October. This appointment comes as a surprise, as Cavanagh was initially expected to continue his CFO duties alongside his new presidency.

title: Sony: Japanese Emperor With Diversified Growth (NYSE:SONY)
summary: Sony Group Corporation is a multinational technology titan with a highly diversified business model, excelling in gaming with PlayStation, camera sensors, and music. The company has shown strong growth across most segments in Q2 FY22 and is considered undervalued both intrinsically and relative to historic multiples. This article breaks down Sony's business model, financials, and valuation, highlighting its leadership in various technology sectors.

title: ATCO acquires $713M wind, solar portfolio from Suncor
summary: ATCO has acquired a $713 million wind and solar energy portfolio from Suncor Energy Inc. in Alberta and Ontario, significantly boosting its renewable energy focus. Concurrently, ATCO signed a 15-year renewable energy purchase agreement with Microsoft Corporation, through which Microsoft will purchase 150 MW of clean energy from ATCO’s newly acquired Forty Mile Wind Phase 1 Project in Alberta. This acquisition aligns with ATCO's goal to become a leader in decarbonization and increase its renewable energy capacity to over 1,000 MW by 2030, with a net-zero greenhouse gas emissions target by 2050.

title: China’s NetEase buys Halo co-developer SkyBox Labs in global expansion drive
summary: NetEase, China's second-largest video games company, has acquired Canadian gaming studio SkyBox Labs, known for co-developing popular titles such as "Halo Infinite" and "Minecraft." This acquisition is part of NetEase's aggressive global expansion strategy, following a previous acquisition of French studio Quantic Dream and increased regulatory scrutiny in China's gaming market. The move comes after Activision Blizzard ended its partnership with NetEase and highlights NetEase's focus on growing its international revenue and in-house game development capabilities.

title: 2023 Blue Arc e-Van First Drive: An Anti-Startup Goes Electric
summary: The 2023 Blue Arc electric van, developed by the Shyft Group, represents a modern approach to last-mile delivery vehicles, stemming from an established manufacturer rather than a startup. It features a unique Dana E-Axle for efficiency, innovative leaf spring suspension for ride comfort, and a driver-focused interior with advanced technology. Production is set to begin in July 2023, with pricing between $165,000 and $185,000, aiming to meet the growing demand for electric delivery solutions.

title: WPP strengthens Salesforce expertise with Fenom Digital acquisition
summary: WPP has acquired Fenom Digital, a digital transformation agency specializing in Salesforce solutions, to bolster Wunderman Thompson's e-commerce capabilities. This acquisition aligns with a trend of agencies expanding their e-commerce offerings, particularly those with strong Salesforce ties, as online retail continues to grow. The move aims to enhance client services across multiple Salesforce clouds, despite recent economic struggles for Salesforce itself.

title: DXC Technology Identifies Five Cybersecurity Trends that will Impact Life and Business in 2023 and Beyond
summary: DXC Technology has identified five key cybersecurity trends for 2023 and beyond, including an acceleration of the cybersecurity arms race with AI, increased risks in the metaverse, and a rise in geopolitical cyberattacks. The company also predicts that critical national infrastructure will be a growing target for cyber adversaries and highlights the increasing career opportunities within the cybersecurity sector due to a significant global talent shortfall.

title: Are You Ready To Step Up To B2B Marketing’s New Destiny?
summary: B2B marketing is undergoing a significant transformation due to changes in buyer behavior, disruptive business models, and rapid technology evolution. Marketers must shift from traditional roles to a broader purpose focused on customer value and sustainable business growth. This requires strategic mindset shifts from product-centricity to customer outcomes, funnel to buyer's journey, and acquisition to lifecycle relationship management, emphasizing personalized, data-driven, and trust-building engagements.

title: Intel Launches 4th Gen Xeon Scalable Processors, Max Series CPUs and GPUs
summary: Intel has launched its 4th Gen Xeon Scalable processors, along with the Intel Xeon CPU Max Series and Intel Data Center GPU Max Series. These new processors aim to deliver significant improvements in performance, efficiency, and capabilities for AI, cloud, network, edge, and high-performance computing, emphasizing built-in accelerators and sustainability features. The company highlights broad industry adoption and performance gains across various key workloads.

title: Intel 4th Gen Xeon series offers a leap in data center performance and efficiency
summary: Intel has launched its 4th Gen Intel Xeon scalable processors, including the Intel Xeon CPU Max Series and Intel Data Center GPU Max Series, featuring enhanced security and new AI capabilities. These processors promise significant improvements in data center performance and efficiency, offering workload-first acceleration and optimized software for better total cost of ownership. The new line boasts built-in accelerators, power savings, and expanded confidential computing features designed to address critical computing challenges and sustainability goals.

title: Networked Quantum Computers: IonQ Acquires Assets of Entangled Networks
summary: IonQ, Inc. (NYSE: IONQ) announced its acquisition of the operating assets of Entangled Networks Ltd., a Toronto-based company specializing in distributed quantum processors. This acquisition, IonQ's first, is intended to further IonQ's goal of building large-scale quantum computers by enabling computation across multiple distributed quantum processors and strengthens IonQ's international presence with the launch of IonQ Canada. The Entangled Networks team will join IonQ, contributing expertise in quantum architecture and software tools to enhance system performance.

title: IonQ acquires quantum networking startup Entangled Networks
summary: IonQ Inc. has acquired Entangled Networks Ltd., a startup specializing in networking technology for linking quantum processors, for an undisclosed sum. This acquisition aims to advance IonQ's goal of building more advanced quantum systems with multiple processors by leveraging Entangled Networks' optical interconnect hardware and MultiQopt compiler software. The integration of Entangled Networks' expertise and tools is expected to lead to substantial performance improvements in IonQ's quantum hardware and support the development of prototype multi-processor systems this year.

title: The 7 Best Mutual Funds for Your 401k
summary: This article identifies seven top mutual funds suitable for 401k accounts, emphasizing their diversification benefits, low fees, and potential for weathering market downturns. It details each fund, including their holdings, expense ratios, performance, and minimum investment requirements, covering sectors from energy and technology to emerging markets and precious metals. The piece aims to guide investors in selecting robust options for their retirement savings.

title: Resilient Retail
summary: In this article, Shelley Bransten, Corporate Vice President, Global Industry Solutions at Microsoft, discusses the concept of "Resilient Retail" and how digital technology is crucial for retailers to thrive amid economic, societal, and technological changes. Microsoft commissioned a study with Futurum Research, surveying 1,200 retailers, which identified key characteristics of resilient retailers, including a focus on customer experience, empowering frontline workers, and leveraging advanced technologies like AI and smart store analytics. The article also introduces two new Microsoft Cloud for Retail capabilities: Smart Store Analytics and Store Operations Assist, aimed at digitizing physical stores and enhancing the frontline worker experience.

title: Collective intelligence exponentially outperforms any one person or idea:" An interview with N-able's John Pagliuca
summary: John Pagliuca, CEO of N-able, discusses his support for Computing's Women in Tech Excellence Campaign, emphasizing the critical need for more women in the tech industry at all levels. He shares his career journey into IT and offers advice for women looking to enter or advance in tech, highlighting the importance of mentorship, continuous learning, and embracing uncomfortable challenges for growth. Pagliuca stresses that collective intelligence surpasses individual ideas and leaders should foster environments that encourage diverse feedback.

title: Thousands reportedly laid off at Cloud Software Group, the parent company of Citrix
summary: Cloud Software Group, the parent company of Citrix Systems, NetScaler, and Tibco Software, has reportedly laid off thousands of employees, including much of Citrix's commercial sales organization and other key departments. This mass layoff, described as the largest in Citrix's history, comes after Citrix went private in September 2022 following its acquisition by Evergreen Coast Capital and Vista Equity Partners for $16.5 billion. The layoffs reflect a broader trend of job cuts within the tech industry amidst a challenging global economy.

title: Cognizant appoints ex-Infosys president Ravi Kumar as CEO
summary: Cognizant has appointed former Infosys President Ravi Kumar S as its new Chief Executive Officer and a member of the Board, effective immediately. Kumar, who previously served as President of Cognizant Americas after leaving Infosys, succeeds Brian Humphries. The company also announced that Stephen J. Rohleder was elected Chair of the Board and anticipates reporting strong fourth-quarter and annual revenue results for 2022.

title: Meta faces a future of more legal woes and falling revenues
summary: Meta, formerly Facebook, is experiencing significant challenges including plummeting stock value, falling revenues, and increasing regulatory scrutiny, a situation that worsened after its rebrand in October 2021. Despite investor concerns and substantial losses from its metaverse division, Reality Labs, CEO Mark Zuckerberg remains committed to heavy investment in the metaverse. The company also faces ongoing legal battles, hefty fines for data privacy breaches, and a class-action lawsuit settlement, exacerbating doubts about its future prospects.

title: Buffett-Backed Taiwan Semiconductor Braces for Chip-Sector Downturn
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) reported record profits for its fourth quarter, exceeding analyst expectations, but also issued a warning about a potential downturn in demand for 2023. This news comes as the company, backed by Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway, indicates higher costs for building facilities in the U.S. compared to Taiwan. TSMC is preparing for a challenging period in the chip sector despite its strong recent financial performance.

title: Google, Nvidia Express Concerns to FTC About Microsoft’s Activision Deal
summary: Google and Nvidia have joined Sony in expressing concerns to the Federal Trade Commission regarding Microsoft's proposed $69 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard. These concerns further support the FTC's lawsuit to block the deal, citing potential harm to competition in the video-game industry. The FTC has scheduled an in-house trial for August to address these issues.

title: Oracle jumps into payments for retailers
summary: Oracle has expanded its services for retailers to include in-store payment acceptance, offering tap-to-pay capabilities for various payment methods like debit, credit, Apple, Google, and Samsung digital wallets. This new feature, which became available in December, will be sold at a fixed fee without long-term contracts or minimum monthly payment volumes. Oracle aims to provide a more stable and cost-effective "payment to processing" solution, integrating it with their existing hardware and cloud-based software for inventory and staff management.

title: Banco de Chile y SKY suman nuevos beneficios para sus clientes
summary: Banco de Chile and SKY Airline have expanded their "Travel SKY" program, introducing new benefits for a wider range of Banco de Chile customers, effective January 18, 2023. Previously exclusive to high-tier credit card holders, now Platinum and Dorada credit card users, debit card holders, and Cuenta FAN users can also access preferential counter and boarding via "Starpass." Additionally, these new beneficiaries will receive a 40% discount on baggage or favorite seat purchases, valid until June 30, 2023.

title: Biometric Sensors Market Size to Touch USD 3.5829 million by 2030 According to Acumen Research and Consulting
summary: The global biometric sensors market is projected to grow from USD 1.3195 million in 2021 to USD 3.5829 million by 2030, exhibiting a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 11.9% from 2022 to 2030. This growth is driven by increasing demand for secure authentication, advancements in technology, and wider adoption in various sectors like healthcare, banking, and government. Despite its growth, the market faces challenges due to lack of standardization, high implementation costs, and privacy concerns.

title: Rio Tinto Lowers Production Forecast for Diavik Mine
summary: Rio Tinto has lowered its 2023 production forecast for the Diavik diamond mine in Canada due to undisclosed reasons. The company now expects to produce 3.0m to 3.8m carats, a significant reduction from its 2022 forecast of 4.5m to 5.0m carats, although actual 2022 production met targets. Rio Tinto has held 100% ownership of the mine since November 2021, and the mine is slated to close in 2025.

title: World Economic Forum Establishes Purpose-driven Metaverse to Tackle World’s Most Pressing Challenges
summary: The World Economic Forum, in collaboration with Accenture and Microsoft, has launched its Global Collaboration Village, a purpose-driven metaverse designed to address global challenges. This initiative brings together 80 leading organizations and will host its first multilateral session during the Annual Meeting 2023 in Davos. The Village aims to foster more inclusive and sustained global cooperation through immersive virtual spaces using Microsoft Mesh technology.

title: The January 2023 Patch Tuesday Security Update Review
summary: The January 2023 Patch Tuesday brought a significant volume of security updates from Microsoft and Adobe. Microsoft released 98 patches, 11 critical, addressing vulnerabilities across various products, including one actively exploited and one publicly known. Adobe issued four patches covering 29 vulnerabilities, with 15 critical fixes for Reader, and several others for Dimension, InCopy, and InDesign. The article also highlights end-of-support products like Windows 7, Windows Server 2008, and R2, urging users to upgrade to newer versions for continued security.

title: TD SYNNEX Unveils New Fraud Defense Solution to Combat Widespread Security Risks
summary: TD SYNNEX has launched a new fraud defense solution, the SMB Fraud Defense Click-to-Run™ solution, which integrates Microsoft Azure services to combat increasing cloud-based security threats for small and medium businesses. This solution aims to elevate security postures through phishing prevention, proactive alerts, and warning signals, leveraging Microsoft Azure Active Directory and cost management features. The company emphasizes the growing cyber and security threats, highlighting the need for advanced solutions to protect businesses from significant financial losses due to cybercrime.

title: Microsoft to shed 10,000 jobs, adding to glut of tech layoffs
summary: Microsoft announced it would eliminate 10,000 jobs and take a $1.2 billion charge to earnings as cloud-computing customers reduce spending and the company prepares for a potential recession. Despite this, Microsoft plans to increase investment in generative artificial intelligence, seen as a new growth area. The layoffs, affecting less than 5% of its workforce, are expected to conclude by the end of March, though strategic hiring will continue.

title: nCino lays off 7% of workforce, CFO exits
summary: Fintech company nCino, headquartered in Wilmington, laid off nearly 7% of its workforce, impacting over 100 employees, due to a fluctuating market and the company's shift towards profitable growth. The layoffs occurred on the same day CFO David Rudow's exit was announced, with Greg Orenstein stepping in as his replacement. Affected employees will receive a severance package, and the company has mandated a return-to-office policy, citing in-person collaboration benefits.

title: Rubrik grows fast, ex-CEO of Palo Alto Networks joins board
summary: Rubrik has reached a significant milestone, announcing over $500 million in annual recurring revenue from software subscriptions. The company, which specializes in backup solutions, also welcomed Mark McLaughlin, the former CEO of Palo Alto Networks, to its board of directors. This growth and strategic board appointment underscore Rubrik's strengthened position in the cybersecurity market amidst rising cybercrime.

title: Author: Bhagya Ayyavoo
summary: This page serves as an archive for articles written by Bhagya Ayyavoo for Sify.com. It highlights her role as an author and host for a podcast discussing "Toxic Leadership at workplace…" from January 18, 2023. The podcast features an all-women panel examining toxic management styles and whether women contribute to workplace toxicity.

title: GroupM confirms layoffs of staffers across N. America, EMEA regions
summary: GroupM, the largest media agency, is conducting layoffs across its global network, impacting 114 to 126 employees in North America and EMEA regions. These cutbacks are attributed to a realignment of roles following mergers within GroupM last April, including the formation of EssenceMediacom and GroupM Nexus. The timing also coincides with an economic downturn and recent client losses, although GroupM states the reductions are part of internal "hygiene" and not as extensive as those seen in Big Tech.

title: Wednesday's Top Analyst Upgrades and Downgrades: BP, Exxon Mobil, Kroger, Microsoft, RingCentral, Wayfair, Wendy's and More
summary: This article compiles top analyst upgrades, downgrades, and initiations from Wednesday, January 18, 2023, for various major companies including BP, Exxon Mobil, Kroger, Microsoft, RingCentral, and Wayfair. It highlights current market conditions, including higher futures trading, ongoing Q4 earnings reports impacting S&P 500 companies, and movements in Treasury yields, oil prices, natural gas, and cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin. Analysts are keenly focused on guidance for the upcoming quarters, with expectations of potential full-year earnings forecast adjustments.

title: Getty Images suing the makers of popular AI art tool for allegedly stealing photos
summary: Getty Images has filed a lawsuit against Stability AI, the creator of the AI art tool Stable Diffusion, alleging copyright infringement. The stock image company claims Stability AI copied and processed millions of its images without obtaining proper licenses. This action highlights the growing tension between traditional media suppliers and AI art generators, as artists become concerned about their work being used for AI training without credit.

title: Sobre a J.B. Hunt Transport, Inc.
summary: J.B. Hunt Transport, Inc., uma líder em transporte da Fortune 500, migrou suas cargas de trabalho de nuvem para otimizar o desempenho e a eficiência. A empresa utilizou o IBM Turbonomic para gerenciar recursos, resultando em 2.000 ações de redimensionamento e uma economia de 650 horas anuais, além de uma migração bem-sucedida do Azure para o Google Cloud com tempo de inatividade zero. A solução também auxilia na otimização contínua e na colaboração para reduzir o desperdício em ambientes de contêineres e na automação de ações não disruptivas.

title: Who the heck paid $100,000 for an old Twitter logo statue in Elon Musk's auction?
summary: A three-and-a-half-foot tall statue of Twitter's bird logo was sold for $100,000 at an online auction held by Heritage Global Partners, which is managing the sale of surplus office items from Twitter. The identity of the buyer remains unknown as the auction house declined to comment. This auction is part of Elon Musk's efforts to cut costs since acquiring Twitter for $44 billion and has also included other items like a neon Twitter logo and industrial kitchen equipment.

title: AI Time: 10 Ways Artificial Intelligence is Getting Real
summary: A new report from Citi Global Insights highlights 10 areas of innovation in Artificial Intelligence, a market that has grown significantly at a 35% CAGR since 2015. The article discusses key AI technologies such as Large Language Models, AI Art, Quantum for AI, Edge AI, and Explainable AI, detailing their market potential and impact. It also features insights from leading AI experts on the future trajectory of AI development.

title: Cotações de BDRs: Bolsa de Valores ao Vivo e últimas notícias
summary: This article provides live BDR (Brazilian Depositary Receipts) quotes and the latest financial news from Money Times. It features an extensive list of BDRs available for trading, along with recent news touching on BDR recommendations from financial institutions like BTG Pactual and Empiricus, B3 trading volumes, and company updates that impact BDRs. The content caters to investors interested in international stocks through the Brazilian stock exchange.

title: A new way of selling cruises; VR gains new friends; the sector that ‘knows too much’ but not enough; cruise ships get TikTok - WiT
summary: This article covers several innovations in the travel industry, including the launch of Cruisebound, a new online travel agency for cruises targeting younger travelers with a mobile-first approach. It also discusses the increasing role of virtual reality in travel planning and highlights a digital perception gap between airline executives and customers regarding innovation. Lastly, it notes that Carnival Corp. and Royal Caribbean Group are rolling out faster internet, including Starlink, across their fleets to support social media use like TikTok.

title: Bitcoin Could Be on Precipice of New Bull Market
summary: Bitcoin's strong start to 2023 has led some observers to believe it could be on the verge of a new bull market, potentially benefiting crypto-correlated ETFs like the Invesco Alerian Galaxy Blockchain Users and Decentralized Commerce ETF (BLKC). While historical patterns suggest a significant rally, future gains may not match the extreme percentages of previous cycles. BLKC also holds quality and value stocks, which could provide stability and support its performance.

title: Best 12 Freelancing Sites in India
summary: The article lists and describes the top 12 freelancing websites available to workers in India, recognizing the significant increase in freelancers and the expanding gig economy. It highlights various platforms, noting whether they are national or internationally recognized, and details their unique features, typical job offerings, and how freelancers can engage with them. The platforms cater to a wide range of skills and experience levels, from beginners to specialized professionals.

title: Global X S&p 500 Covered Call Etf Share Price
summary: This article provides detailed financial information for the Global X S&P 500 Covered Call ETF (XYLD), including its current share price, performance metrics, historical returns, and fundamental data like expense ratio and AUM. It also lists the top holdings, sector breakdown, market cap distribution, and offers insights on its performance against peers and market cap movements. The article concludes with an FAQ section on investing in XYLD from India.

title: PNC Financial Services Group Inc. stock underperforms Thursday when compared to competitors
summary: PNC Financial Services Group Inc. (PNC) stock fell 2.66% on Thursday, closing at $148.02, underperforming the broader market downturn as the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also declined. This marked the fourth consecutive day of losses for PNC, and its competitors like JPMorgan Chase & Co., Bank of America Corp., and Wells Fargo & Co. experienced smaller percentage drops. The trading volume for PNC shares also significantly exceeded its 50-day average.

title: Do Companies Need to Shake Up the Way They Find Tech Talent?
summary: This article argues that traditional recruiting practices need an overhaul, especially in the tech sector, to foster diversity of thought and innovation. It highlights JPMorgan Chase's initiatives, such as the Tech Connect program and Autism at Work, which recruit individuals from non-traditional backgrounds, demonstrating how valuing unique perspectives can drive success. The piece emphasizes that diverse teams lead to greater innovation and better hiring decisions.

title: 100-Year-Old Retailer Canadian Tire Modernizes Data Platform with Azure Synapse Analytics and Power BI
summary: Canadian Tire Corporation (CTC) is modernizing its data platform using Azure Synapse Analytics and Power BI to achieve near-real-time insights and data-driven decision-making. The retailer aims to consolidate its data ecosystem, streamline architecture from nine steps to five, and empower self-service across the organization. This shift will allow CTC to revolutionize its operations, better serve customers, and enhance its omnichannel experience.

title: A Survival Guide for When You’ve Been Laid Off
summary: This article offers a survival guide for individuals who have been laid off, acknowledging the increasing prevalence of job cuts across various sectors, including tech giants and financial institutions. It emphasizes the importance of having a plan in place, even though layoffs can be unpredictable. The article aims to help individuals cope and navigate the next steps after losing their job.

title: Israeli Game Maker Playtika To Offer 683M Euros For Rovio Studios Acquisition
summary: Playtika Holding Corp has increased its offer to acquire Finnish game maker Rovio, known for its "Angry Birds" franchise, to 683 million euros. This new offer values each Rovio share at 9.05 euros, a significant premium over its recent closing price. The acquisition highlights ongoing consolidation in the gaming industry, especially as the mobile game market experiences a slowdown.

title: D-Wave Highlights Commercial Customer Engagements, Cross-Platform Product Enhancements
summary: D-Wave announced new commercial customer engagements and product updates for its annealing and gate model quantum computing solutions at its Qubits 2023 user conference. The company highlighted real-world applications with customers like Mastercard and Davidson Technologies, demonstrating the growing commercial adoption of quantum-hybrid solutions. D-Wave also shared significant progress on its next-generation Advantage2™ annealing system and advancements in its gate model platform, emphasizing its commitment to delivering diverse quantum solutions.

title: Here are the layoff severance packages Google, Microsoft, Amazon and other tech giants have promised
summary: As major tech companies like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon announce significant layoffs, this article compares the severance packages offered by these and other tech giants like Meta, Salesforce, and Twitter. The packages vary widely, from Google's 16-week base severance plus additional weeks per year of service to Amazon's 60-day full pay period followed by several weeks of severance. The article highlights the differing approaches to severance, health benefits, and stock vesting amidst an uncertain job market for laid-off tech workers.

title: Amazon, Microsoft Job Cuts Deal Another Blow to Ailing Seattle
summary: Job cuts at Amazon and Microsoft are impacting Seattle, America's second-largest tech hub, which is already struggling to recover from the pandemic's blow to its commuter economy. While the 28,000 global job losses might seem small for the region's 2.1 million workforce, this development is a significant psychological setback, making investors and businesses hesitant about new projects and expansion. This further exacerbates the economic challenges faced by the city.

title: Amazon to Plow Extra $35 Billion Into Virginia Data Centers in Cloud Race
summary: Amazon's cloud unit, Amazon Web Services (AWS), plans to invest an additional $35 billion in new data centers in Virginia by 2040. This move aims to reinforce its leading position against competitors like Microsoft and Alphabet. The expansion is expected to create 1,000 jobs in the state, which is a crucial hub for AWS operations.

title: Stripe becomes a strategic payments partner for Amazon
summary: Amazon is significantly broadening its use of Stripe's payment processing platform, making Stripe a strategic payments partner across various Amazon business units in the US, Europe, and Canada. In return, Stripe will expand its utilization of Amazon Web Services (AWS), focusing on AWS Graviton chips and Nitro Enclaves for enhanced performance and security. This expanded partnership builds on an existing relationship, with Stripe set to handle a substantial portion of Amazon's transaction volume.

title: Silicon Valley 2.0? 5 US cities that could be the new tech start-up central
summary: Several southern US cities are emerging as new tech hubs, drawing companies like Tesla, Apple, Oracle, Microsoft, and Google away from California's Silicon Valley. High tax rates, labor costs, regulations, and a declining quality of life in Silicon Valley are pushing these companies to look for more affordable and business-friendly environments in states such as Texas, Arizona, Georgia, and Florida. These new tech centers offer incentives, lower costs of living, and new luxury residential developments to accommodate the influx of workers.

title: Spotify to slash 6% of workforce, adding to tech layoffs glut | Daily Sabah
summary: Spotify announced it will lay off 6% of its 10,000 employees, amounting to about 600 people, as the music streaming giant prepares for a possible recession and aligns costs with revenue growth. CEO Daniel Ek admitted he was "too ambitious in investing ahead of our revenue growth." This move follows similar layoffs across the tech sector, including Google, Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft, as companies face economic headwinds and a downturn in demand after pandemic-driven growth.

title: Microsoft and OpenAI extend partnership
summary: Microsoft and OpenAI are extending their partnership with a multiyear, multibillion-dollar investment to accelerate AI breakthroughs. This agreement will expand their collaboration in AI supercomputing and research, allowing both companies to independently commercialize advanced AI technologies. Microsoft will integrate OpenAI's models into its products and Azure will remain OpenAI's exclusive cloud provider, powering all its workloads.

title: Ansys Inc. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Ansys Inc. (ANSS) saw its stock rise by 1.70% to $260.79 on a strong trading day, outperforming both the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average. This marks the second consecutive day of gains for the company, though its stock value remains $82.07 below its 52-week high. Competitors Microsoft, Oracle, and IBM also experienced gains on the same day.

title: News | King Charles's Property Company 'Sues' Twitter Over Unpaid Rent
summary: King Charles's property company, the Crown Estate, has filed a lawsuit against Twitter in the High Court in London for alleged unpaid rent at its London headquarters in the West End. This action comes as Twitter, under Elon Musk's ownership, reportedly ceased paying rent at its global offices to cut costs. The Crown Estate seeks recovery of rent arrears, interest, and costs, with a legal expert suggesting summary judgment could be sought if Twitter lacks a valid defense.

title: What's Changed: 2023 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Low-Code Application Platforms
summary: Gartner has released its 2023 Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Low-Code Application Platforms (LCAPs), evaluating 17 significant providers based on updated criteria reflecting market trends. The report categorizes vendors into Leaders, Challengers, Visionaries, and Niche Players, with new additions like Alibaba and Huawei. It highlights key strengths and differentiated offerings of each platform, including Mendix, OutSystems, Microsoft, Salesforce, Oracle, Appian, and Zoho.

title: Understanding the value of an ESG audit certification
summary: The article highlights the increasing importance of ESG audit certification for companies due to growing stakeholder demand, new regulations, and rising ESG investments. It emphasizes that third-party assurance of ESG reporting builds trust and differentiation for firms, noting that a significant percentage of investors believe sustainability disclosures should be as rigorously audited as financial statements. The piece also positions ESG specialization as a growth opportunity for accounting firms, allowing them to attract and better serve clients.

title: Oracle Corp. stock rises Tuesday, outperforms market
summary: Oracle Corp. (ORCL) shares rose 0.82% to $89.70 on Tuesday, outperforming the broader market which saw mixed trading with the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising and the S&P 500 falling. The stock achieved a new 52-week high and outperformed competitors like Microsoft and Alphabet. Trading volume was slightly below its 50-day average.

title: Bp powers greater innovations with a modular data mesh design on Azure
summary: Global energy company bp is transforming into an integrated multi-source energy provider by adopting a modular data mesh architecture on Microsoft Azure. This initiative aims to democratize data ownership, enhance data sharing, and optimize platform flexibility, accelerating innovations. By leveraging the Microsoft Intelligent Data Platform, bp is creating a scalable and secure data ecosystem for its diverse global operations.

title: Bad Week of Earnings Pulls Q4 Growth Rate Lower
summary: The S&P 500's blended EPS growth for Q4 decreased to -4.6% due to a week of mixed earnings reports from major financial institutions and other companies. This marks the lowest growth rate in over two years, driven by factors like increased loan loss provisions and consumer credit deterioration. Despite the decline, the earnings season is picking up, with key companies like Microsoft, Tesla, IBM, and Intel expected to report, and some companies like Danaher and Weyerhaeuser signaling positive results.

title: Five Proven Ways That DEX Tools Can Save You Money In 2023
summary: Despite economic pressures and widespread layoffs, companies should not cut back on Digital Employee Experience (DEX) investments. While traditionally used for employee engagement, DEX tools can immediately save money through tactical use cases such as instant visibility, proactive asset management, automated remediation, improved boot-up times, and license reclamation. These cost-saving benefits can help justify continued funding for DEX initiatives, allowing companies to pursue longer-term goals like enhanced customer and employee experience.

title: Gartner Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Low-Code Application Platforms 2023
summary: Gartner has released its 2023 Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Low-Code Application Platforms (LCAPs), identifying 17 competitors and defining LCAP solutions as tools for rapid custom application development with minimal coding. The report categorizes vendors into Leaders (OutSystems, Mendix, Microsoft, Salesforce, ServiceNow), Challengers (Oracle), Visionaries (Appian, Zoho, Pegasystems), and Niche Players (Retool, Unqork, Huawei, Creatio, Newgen, Alibaba, Kintone, Quickbase). It provides an overview of each vendor's strengths and weaknesses, noting new additions to the Quadrant and anticipating increased demand for low-code platforms as businesses seek to streamline application development.

title: 5 Interesting Learnings from ServiceNow at $8 Billion in ARR
summary: This article analyzes ServiceNow's continued strong performance, reaching $8 billion in ARR with consistent 25% annual growth, despite broader economic headwinds. Key insights include steady gross renewal rates of 98-99%, over 1,500 customers with $1M+ ACV, and high revenue per employee, showcasing its resilience and profitability. The author highlights the effectiveness of long-term contracts and the significant expansion of customer ACV over time.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang: AI is creating tools that will need regulation
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang believes that the powerful new tools developed through artificial intelligence will necessitate regulation. This statement highlights the growing concern among technology leaders about the societal impact of AI innovation. The article briefly touches upon the challenges governments and societies face in adapting to this rapid technological advancement.

title: Financial services firms investing in AI for digital future
summary: A new report by Broadridge Financial Solutions indicates that the majority of financial services firms see AI and other digital transformation technologies as crucial for their strategic future. Firms are accelerating investment in digital transformation, with 27% of their IT budget now allocated to it, up from 16% in 2022. This investment is driven by the belief that digital leadership leads to higher revenue growth, better talent retention, and a modernised tech stack within the next decade.

title: Comcast Corp. nods to new Frisco park and sees ‘great momentum’ in theme parks business
summary: Comcast Corp. highlighted its new kids-oriented Universal theme park planned for Frisco and a horror attraction for Las Vegas during its quarterly financial results call. CEO Brian Roberts stated these new parks are innovative ways to utilize their intellectual properties from DreamWorks and Illumination, extending the brand and fueling growth across all Universal parks. The company saw a significant 49.3% increase in theme park revenue last year, reaching $7.5 billion, and anticipates continued momentum in this sector.

title: Chipotle Plans to Hire 15,000 People Ahead of ‘Burrito Season’
summary: Chipotle Mexican Grill announced plans to hire 15,000 new workers in anticipation of its busiest period, dubbed "burrito season," which runs from March to May. This hiring spree contrasts with other large companies that are implementing layoffs. The company aims to nearly double its North American outlets to 7,000 and needs more staff to support this aggressive growth and manage increased sales during the spring.

title: How Quantum Computing Will Transform Our World
summary: Quantum computing, while still developing, promises to revolutionize various fields by processing information at an exponentially faster rate than traditional computers. Companies like IBM are leading the charge, developing advanced quantum processors and exploring applications in areas like finance, materials science, and AI. However, this transformative technology also presents significant national security risks, particularly concerning the obsolescence of current cryptography, prompting a global race to develop quantum-safe security measures.

title: IBM to cut 3,900 jobs amid broader tech slowdown: WSJ
summary: IBM has announced it will cut approximately 3,900 jobs, stemming from its Kyndryl Holdings spin-off and healthcare divestiture, incurring a $300 million charge. This move comes as the technology sector experiences a slowdown in spending, impacting companies like Microsoft as well. Despite flat sales in the fourth quarter due to a strong US dollar, IBM reported increased adjusted earnings per share and expects mid-single-digit adjusted revenue growth for 2023.

title: Intel shares drop on weak quarterly results and expectations for another quarter of losses
summary: Intel's shares fell after the company reported weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter results and provided a soft forecast for the first quarter of 2023. The chipmaker experienced a significant decline in revenue for the fourth consecutive quarter due to a downturn in PC chip sales and broader economic headwinds. The company also announced a net loss for Q4 and anticipates further losses in Q1, leading to concerns about its financial performance in the near future.

title: Flying high: How ORIX Aviation has built a stellar track record in aviation investment
summary: This article highlights ORIX Aviation's success as a leading aircraft leasing company, detailing its robust business model, consistent profitability, and significant market position. It discusses the critical role of aircraft leasing in global aviation and ORIX Aviation's commitment to sustainable aviation, including active involvement in developing Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and exploring new technologies like hydrogen-powered and electric aircraft.

title: SAP to lay off 3,000 and sell Qualtrics stake as profits plunge
summary: SAP SE announced plans to lay off 3,000 employees, representing 2.5% of its global workforce, following a significant drop in net profit for the fourth quarter of 2022. The company also intends to sell its 84% stake in Qualtrics International Inc., which it acquired for $8 billion in 2019. Despite the profit decline, SAP aims for double-digit operating profit growth in 2023, driven by its shift to cloud-based solutions like S/4HANA and the "Rise with SAP" digital transformation program.

title: SAP plans layoffs and selloff with cloud revenue up but profit down
summary: SAP announced layoffs impacting 2,800 staff and plans to sell its remaining stake in Qualtrics to re-focus on its core business. This restructuring comes despite an 11% overall revenue increase and a 33% surge in cloud revenue in 2022, as net income dropped significantly by 68%. The company aims to invest further in integrated industry-specific solutions and expects continued strong cloud revenue growth.

title: IBM, SAP latest to slash workforce
summary: IBM announced it would cut 1.5% of its global workforce, approximately 3,900 employees, despite beating revenue expectations, attributing the reductions to previous business unit spinoffs rather than current performance. This move follows similar workforce reductions by other major tech companies like Microsoft, Google, and Salesforce, as the sector navigates economic challenges. European software firm SAP also revealed plans to cut 3,000 jobs globally due to declining profits, aiming to refocus on strategic growth.

title: Shutterstock Launches AI Image Generator Using DALL-E’s Technology
summary: Shutterstock has integrated OpenAI's DALL-E into its platform, launching an AI image generator available globally to its customers. The tool, part of Shutterstock's Creative Flow, aims to make design accessible to everyone and is built on ethically sourced datasets. Shutterstock also revealed a revenue-sharing model that will compensate contributors whose content was used in training the AI models.

title: Swiss Industrial Company Georg Fischer (GF) Taps DXC Technology to Transform the Workplace
summary: DXC Technology has secured a multi-year contract with Swiss industrial company Georg Fischer (GF) to digitalize the work experience for its global workforce. Through a five-year agreement, DXC will implement cloud-based solutions utilizing Microsoft and ServiceNow technologies to create a centralized digital hub, enhancing collaboration and data-driven decision-making for GF's 15,000 employees across 34 countries. This modernization will also improve IT issue management and productivity for GF.

title: IBM Is Tech’s Most Beaten-Down Company
summary: This article argues that IBM has significantly fallen from its former prominence, ranking 49th on the Fortune 500 compared to 8th in 1980. Its recent financial results show flat revenue and modest net income, trailing far behind other tech giants like Apple, Amazon, and Microsoft. The author criticizes IBM for missing key technological advancements such as cloud computing, search, e-commerce, and operating systems despite its past R&D capabilities.

title: ServiceNow CEO: Our Ambition Is to Be the Defining Enterprise Software Company of the 21st Century
summary: ServiceNow's CEO, Bill McDermott, articulated the company's ambition to become "the defining enterprise software company of the 21st century" during its Q4 2022 earnings call. The company reported strong financial results with total revenue of $1,940 million and subscription revenue growth of 20% and 22% year-over-year respectively. ServiceNow also emphasized its transition towards becoming a platform company, aiming to capitalize on a $500 billion market opportunity with its Now Platform.

title: Dow Chemical to cut 2,000 jobs
summary: Dow Chemical announced Thursday it will cut approximately 2,000 jobs from its workforce as part of a plan to achieve $1 billion in cost savings in 2023. The company has been battling soaring energy costs following the Russian invasion of Ukraine and reported a 17% drop in net sales during the fourth quarter of 2022. This move aligns with a trend of major corporations, particularly in the tech industry, implementing mass layoffs recently.

title: Spotify back up after second outage in two weeks
summary: Spotify experienced a brief outage on Thursday, its second in two weeks, which prevented tens of thousands of users from accessing the music streaming platform. The services have since been restored, with Spotify Status confirming that "Everything's looking much better now." This incident follows a similar disruption earlier in the month and comes amidst other tech giants like Microsoft and Meta also facing recent service interruptions.

title: ArcelorMittal Leads $120 Million Capital Raise for Green Steel Startup Boston Metal
summary: Boston Metal, a green steel startup, has raised $120 million in a funding round led by ArcelorMittal to scale up its zero-emissions Molten Oxide Electrolysis (MOE) technology. The funds will support the production of green steel at its pilot plant, the design of its first green steel plant, and the construction of a commercial plant for high-value metals in Brazil. This investment highlights the growing demand for sustainable steel and the industry's push towards decarbonization, with additional backing from Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund and SiteGround Capital.

title: Microsoft and ArcelorMittal invest in green Boston Steel startup spun out of MIT
summary: Microsoft and ArcelorMittal have invested $120 million in Boston Metal, an MIT-spun startup focused on producing clean steel. Boston Metal, led by CEO Tadeu Carneiro, aims to ramp up green steel production at its Woburn, Massachusetts facility and build a subsidiary in Brazil, with plans for a demonstration plant in 2024 and a commercial plant in 2026. This investment highlights efforts by major corporations to reduce carbon emissions through sustainable industrial alternatives.

title: Is Augmented Reality safe?
summary: Augmented Reality (AR) blends digital information with the real world, raising significant safety concerns despite its benefits. The article highlights potential dangers in privacy, security, and mental health, including data collection, cyber-attacks, and the addictive nature of AR. It emphasizes the need for careful consideration and control as AR technology becomes more integrated into daily life.

title: Too much trust in the cuckoo’s nest
summary: This article reflects on Cliff Stoll's 1989 classic, "The Cuckoo's Egg," highlighting how the book anticipated the concept of zero trust and reveals that typical cyberattack chains have remained surprisingly consistent over three decades. The author connects the historical hacking methods described in the book—like finding attack surfaces, compromising systems with stolen credentials, lateral movement, and data theft—to present-day cybercriminal tactics. It emphasizes the enduring relevance of Stoll's observations on network trust and foreshadows modern cybersecurity challenges, reinforcing the idea that trust in digital environments is a vulnerability.

title: Salesforce appoints new board directors amid activist investor pressure
summary: Salesforce has appointed three new board directors, including hedge fund ValueAct Capital's chief, Mason Morfit, Mastercard CFO Sachin Mehra, and former Carnival Corp CEO Arnold Donald. This move comes amidst increasing pressure from activist investors seeking better cost control and management changes at the cloud-based software firm. While these appointments were planned to enhance operational skills, they also respond to demands from prominent activist investment firms like Elliott Management, Starboard Value, Inclusive Capital, and ValueAct, who have all engaged with Salesforce regarding their concerns.

title: Procter & Gamble CIO: ‘Everybody Must Own the Digital Story’
summary: Procter & Gamble CIO Vittorio Cretella emphasizes the importance of digital transformation across the entire CPG ecosystem to improve customer experiences, build loyalty, and drive growth. He details how P&G leverages technologies like AI, IoT, and cloud computing for everything from product formulation and manufacturing efficiency to consumer engagement and privacy. Cretella also addresses challenges in scaling AI, highlighting the need for integrating data, developing talent, and fostering a culture that embraces automation while prioritizing consumer trust and data privacy.

title: Save $200 on the Sonos Arc Soundbar, now $699 (lowest price ever)
summary: The Sonos Arc Soundbar is currently available for $699, a $200 discount that marks its lowest recorded price, even beating Black Friday deals. This offer from Adorama applies to the white model and is for a limited time. The soundbar was rated 4.5 out of 5 in a hands-on review for its rich sound, substantial bass, and Dolby Atmos support.

title: China's Baidu to launch ChatGPT-style bot in March - source
summary: Chinese internet search giant Baidu Inc is reportedly planning to launch its own artificial intelligence chatbot service, similar to OpenAI's ChatGPT, in March. The service is expected to be a standalone application initially and then integrated into Baidu's search engine, aiming to provide more professional, human-like responses to user queries beyond just links. Baidu has been heavily investing in AI technology to diversify its revenue streams.

title: Apple takes first steps towards 'Made in India' AirPods
summary: Apple has begun manufacturing components for its AirPods in India, marking a significant step towards the "Made in India" initiative for its products beyond the iPhone. Jabil Inc, an Apple supplier, is producing AirPods enclosures in Pune, India, and shipping them to China and Vietnam for assembly. This move is part of Apple's broader strategy to reduce its reliance on Chinese manufacturing and diversify its supply chain.

title: ArcelorMittal and Microsoft Back MIT Green Steel Firm With $120M
summary: Boston Metal, an MIT spinout firm focused on green steel technology, has successfully raised $120 million in a funding round led by ArcelorMittal and with participation from Microsoft. The company's innovative Molten Oxide Electrolysis (MOE) process aims to decarbonize the steel industry, which currently accounts for a significant portion of global carbon emissions. This investment will support Boston Metal in scaling its green steel production at its Woburn, Massachusetts facility and establishing a Brazilian subsidiary for other metal manufacturing.

title: S3 Intelligent-Tiering's Archive Instant Access Tier
summary: Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering now includes an Archive Instant Access (AIA) tier, which automatically moves infrequently accessed data to a more cost-effective storage class while still allowing sub-millisecond retrieval. This tier offers benefits such as no retrieval charges, no minimum storage duration, and zero operational overhead, making it ideal for data with unpredictable access patterns, backups, and log files. NetApp BlueXP Cloud Volumes ONTAP can further extend these benefits by enabling automatic tiering between EBS and S3 Intelligent-Tiering, along with other data management features.

title: Big tech layoffs may ease software engineer shortage
summary: Recent layoffs in the big tech sector, totaling over 228,000 workers since early 2022, are creating a significant influx of software engineers into the job market. This situation presents an opportunity for smaller enterprises to recruit talented individuals, though challenges such as cultural fit and visa costs still exist. Experts suggest that smaller companies can attract talent by offering benefits beyond compensation, including flexibility and the chance for employees to make a greater impact.

title: How a digital retail firm uses enterprise search
summary: Upside, an online retail marketplace, is piloting Glean's enterprise search platform to help its employees efficiently find information across various applications. Glean uses custom language models trained on a customer's specific documents, offering a personalized search experience. The platform has been easy to integrate and has significantly reduced the time employees spend searching for documents, improving overall efficiency.

title: Dr Reddy’s Laboratories to invest in branded markets
summary: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories reported strong Q3FY23 results, with revenue up 27% year-over-year and EBITDA up 70%, driven by strong performance in North America and Russia. The company plans to invest in branded markets in India and other emerging markets to boost core profitability. Analysts maintained a "Buy" rating with an unchanged target price of ₹4,965, citing attractive valuations and potential for re-rating from judicious use of gRevlimid cash flows.

title: Amgen lays off 300, does not disclose whether any are in Thousand Oaks
summary: Amgen, a Thousand Oaks-based biotech company, announced workforce restructuring resulting in approximately 300 layoffs, about 1.3% of its global workforce. The company stated the job cuts are mainly in the commercial team in the United States, but did not specify if any were in its Thousand Oaks headquarters. This follows other major tech companies like Microsoft, Google, and Amazon also announcing significant layoffs, and Amgen released Q4 2022 financial results showing flat revenue and a 15% decrease in net income compared to the previous year.

title: PayPal to lay off 2,000 employees in coming weeks, about 7% of workforce
summary: PayPal announced plans to lay off 2,000 employees, about 7% of its workforce, due to a "challenging macroeconomic environment." CEO Dan Schulman stated the company is focusing resources on core priorities and rightsizing its cost structure. This move follows a trend of recent job cuts across the tech industry, including Google, Microsoft, and Salesforce.

title: AI - opportunity or threat?
summary: The AI revolution, particularly with the advent of DALL-E and ChatGPT, presents both significant opportunities and threats to tech giants and various industries. Companies like Microsoft are heavily investing in AI, while others like Google and social media platforms face challenges to their business models. The article details how AI impacts image design, web development platforms like Wix, the freelancing market through platforms like Fiverr, and even the gaming industry, forcing companies to adapt or risk disruption.

title: Exxon Vaults to Record Annual Profit of $55.7 Billion
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. achieved a record annual profit of $55.7 billion in 2022, marking a significant recovery after suffering losses during the pandemic and a historic proxy fight in 2021. This surge was primarily driven by soaring oil and gas prices globally, allowing Exxon to surpass most major companies in profitability, except for Apple and Microsoft. The company's resurgence reflects a turnaround in its financial performance and market standing.

title: AV for startups and SMEs
summary: This article discusses the importance of effective audio-visual (AV) solutions for startups and SMEs in today's hybrid work environment. It highlights how accessible unified communications and conferencing (UCC) technologies have become, emphasizing simplicity, ubiquity, and flexibility through options like "bring your own device" (BYOD) and platform standardization. The piece also covers advanced AV applications such as meeting equity, digital signage, cloud telephony, and the future role of AR/VR and the Metaverse in business communication.

title: Dole plc offloads US fresh veg division to unit of Chiquita Brands International
summary: Dole plc has sold its fresh vegetables division in the US to Fresh Express, a subsidiary of Chiquita Holdings, for US$293 million. This sale aims to strengthen Dole's financial position and increase its focus on core activities. The transaction, which includes agricultural operations and four processing plants, is subject to US regulatory approval.

title: ACI Worldwide Increases Global Reach, Powering 25 Domestic and Pan-Regional Real-Time Schemes
summary: ACI Worldwide, a leader in real-time payments software, has significantly expanded its global reach, now powering 25 real-time payment schemes across six continents. This expansion includes supporting nine central infrastructures and follows the addition of three new central bank clients in the Middle East in 2022. The company's growth aligns with the global surge in real-time payment adoption, driven by government initiatives and projecting an additional $131 billion in GDP for the top five global real-time markets by 2026.

title: Star Wars Jedi: Survivor delay sends EA shares plunging
summary: Electronic Arts Inc. shares dropped significantly after the company announced a disappointing outlook for the current quarter and a six-week delay for its upcoming game, Star Wars Jedi: Survivor. The delay also prompted EA to lower its fiscal year 2023 bookings outlook. Additionally, EA is ceasing development on mobile versions of its Apex Legends and Battlefield franchises, leading to the closure of Industrial Toys studio and potential job losses.

title: Electronic Arts Cuts Bookings View on ‘Star Wars’ Game Delay, Spending Slowdown
summary: Electronic Arts (EA) has lowered its annual bookings forecast due to a six-week delay in the release of "Star Wars Jedi: Survivor" and a general slowdown in consumer spending. This follows a 4.3% decline in the gaming market in 2022 and comes amidst fears of a continuing industry downturn exacerbated by high inflation and rising interest rates. Analysts note the delay significantly shifts earnings to the next fiscal year.

title: DARPA Collaborating With Atom Computing, Microsoft and PsiQuantum to Develop Utility-Scale Quantum Computers
summary: DARPA has selected Atom Computing, Microsoft, and PsiQuantum to participate in its Underexplored Systems for Utility-Scale Quantum Computing (US2QC) program. The initiative aims to determine if novel quantum computing approaches can achieve utility-scale operations much faster than traditional predictions would suggest. The selected companies will present design concepts for utility-scale quantum computers, which will then undergo rigorous evaluation by a DARPA-led test and validation team.

title: MediaMarktSaturn secures ‘the store of the future’ with Palo Alto Networks portfolio
summary: MediaMarktSaturn, Europe's leading consumer electronics retailer, has partnered with Palo Alto Networks to enhance its cybersecurity infrastructure across over 1,000 stores and online channels. By standardizing on Palo Alto Networks' portfolio, including ML-Powered Next-Generation Firewalls and Prisma Cloud, MediaMarktSaturn aims to create a more secure, agile, and rewarding multichannel shopping experience for its millions of customers, while also improving operational efficiency and innovation for its development teams.

title: Popular video game introduces 'trans-inclusive' character traits, like sex change surgery scars
summary: The Sims 4 has introduced new "trans-inclusive" character options, including binders, shapewear, and "top surgery" scars, sparking both celebration and controversy. While supporters praise the increased representation and inclusivity in the game, critics, including conservative figures, express concerns about the suitability of such content for a game marketed to children as young as 13. Electronic Arts and Maxis state these changes are "purely visual" and do not add new gameplay.

title: 8 reasons this state is the right fit for California companies
summary: Missouri Partnership highlights eight reasons why California companies should consider relocating to Missouri. The article points to lower corporate taxes, a growing talent pool, central geographic access, lower cost of living, natural beauty, and a business-friendly environment as key advantages for businesses seeking to expand or move. It emphasizes Missouri's efforts to foster economic growth and provide a supportive ecosystem for companies.

title: What Was Paul Allen's Net Worth?
summary: This article details Paul Allen's net worth, his journey to becoming a billionaire, and his diverse investment portfolio beyond co-founding Microsoft. It highlights his significant contributions to real estate, art collection, sports team ownership, and various philanthropic endeavors, emphasizing his lasting legacy as a visionary entrepreneur and generous benefactor.

title: HubSpot, Pinterest Add to Tech Layoff Chaos
summary: HubSpot and Pinterest have joined other major tech companies in announcing layoffs, with Pinterest cutting 150 employees (less than 5% of its workforce) and HubSpot letting go of around 500 staff (7% of its total workforce). These cuts reflect a continuing trend of mass layoffs in the tech sector due to a tumultuous 2022 and an uncertain economic climate, with over 82,000 tech workers laid off since the beginning of the year. Companies are implementing various cost-cutting measures, but the stream of layoffs is expected to continue for some time.

title: Matador’s Advance Energy Acquisition Adds Permian Acreage, Takeaway Capacity
summary: Matador Resources Co. has made its largest Permian Basin acquisition to date by agreeing to buy Advance Energy Partners Holdings LLC. The deal includes approximately 18,500 net acres in the northern Delaware Basin and adds about 35 miles of infield gas and water gathering lines, plus three compressor stations to Matador's Pronto Midstream subsidiary. This acquisition provides Matador with significant production, reserves, strategic acreage, and natural gas takeaway capacity to the Waha Hub via the Double E Pipeline.

title: Supermicro Aspires To Be A $10 Billion Server Maker
summary: Supermicro aims to reach $10 billion in annual server sales, a goal that would place it among the top server makers. The company saw explosive growth in 2021 and 2022 due to its self-contained supply chain, which helped it overcome issues faced by competitors and land significant unnamed customers. Supermicro is expanding its manufacturing capabilities globally, including a new campus in Malaysia, to support this ambitious growth target.

title: ChatGPT sets fastest-growing user base record: study
summary: ChatGPT, OpenAI's popular chatbot, reportedly achieved 100 million monthly active users within two months of its launch, making it the fastest-growing consumer application in history, according to a UBS study. This rapid growth, evidenced by 13 million daily unique visitors in January, outpaced TikTok and Instagram. OpenAI has also introduced a US$20 monthly subscription to cover computing costs and offer enhanced services.

title: New DDoS-as-a-Service Platform Attacking Medical Institutions
summary: Passion Group, an affiliate of Killnet and Anonymous Russia, has launched a DDoS-as-a-Service platform. This platform, identified by Radware, was used to target medical institutions in multiple countries as retaliation for supporting Ukraine. The service offers various attack vectors and pricing models, accepting payments in Tether, QIWI, and Bitcoin, and is used by pro-Russian hackers.

title: Allstate moved 95% of its global staff to remote work in one weekend. Here's how
summary: Allstate successfully transitioned 95% of its global workforce to remote work in a single weekend in March 2020 by leveraging existing infrastructure and prioritizing employee well-being. This shift, driven by employee preferences, has led to significant success in recruiting, with applications up 60% and a 30% increase in diverse candidates. The company continues to invest in remote-first strategies, including selling office spaces, redesigning remaining ones, and creating a "workplace futurist" role to adapt to evolving work dynamics.

title: iShares ESG Aware MSCI USA Value ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (BATS:EVUS)
summary: The iShares ESG Aware MSCI USA Value ETF (EVUS) tracks an index of US value stocks with environmental, social, and governance criteria, aiming to maximize ESG exposure. Launched on January 31, 2023, and managed by BlackRock, EVUS has seen its shares increase by 9.9% since the start of the year, trading at $35.25. The ETF has assets under management of $327.13 million, a dividend yield of 1.59%, and top holdings including Microsoft, Micron Technology, and Meta Platforms.

title: Israeli millionaire tech wiz who says his IQ 'lower than any of my peers'
summary: Gili Sahar, a self-made Israeli tech millionaire from Tiberias, details his unconventional path to success, including founding and selling multiple companies like Dicomano and Rubicone. Despite claiming a lower IQ than his peers, he attributes his achievements to high emotional intelligence (EQ), an ability to build relationships, and a stubborn determination, preferring a marathon approach to business and self-funding his ventures. He also shares his unique rural lifestyle, balancing his demanding tech career with a passion for horses and life in the Golan Heights.

title: The 7 most in-demand tech skills for freelancers—many pay more than $125 an hour
summary: Despite recent tech layoffs, the demand for tech skills remains high, creating significant opportunities for freelancers. Career experts and platforms like Upwork highlight a "skills gap" where employers struggle to find talent. This article identifies seven in-demand tech skills for freelancers, including full stack development, mobile app development, web design, UX/UI design, CMS development, manual testing, and scripting/automation, with many commanding hourly rates exceeding $125.

title: EA SPORTS Madden NFL 23 Predicts Philadelphia Eagles To Win Super Bowl LVII 31-17
summary: EA SPORTS Madden NFL 23 has predicted the Philadelphia Eagles to defeat the Kansas City Chiefs 31-17 in Super Bowl LVII, with Jalen Hurts named MVP. The announcement comes as Electronic Arts launches various events and content for football fans leading up to and during Super Bowl week, including gaming tournaments, a Black History Month program, and community events highlighting youth sports. Fans can engage with Madden NFL 23 through special in-game content and live events.

title: Oracle Named a Leader in Two Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ Reports: iPaaS and Data Integration
summary: Oracle has been recognized as a Leader in both the 2023 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Integration Platform as a Service (iPaaS) and the 2022 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Integration Tools. This marks Oracle's sixth consecutive leadership position in iPaaS and fourteenth in data integration. The article highlights Oracle's comprehensive integration capabilities, cost-effectiveness, and ability to address diverse customer needs across various environments.

title: Oracle to invest $1.5 bn in Saudi Arabia, open data centre in Riyadh
summary: Oracle Corp plans to invest $1.5 billion in Saudi Arabia to expand its cloud footprint, including opening a third public cloud region in Riyadh and expanding its existing Jeddah facility. This investment aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 to diversify its economy and attract foreign direct investment, with Oracle also securing contracts for the NEOM project. Saudi officials are pressuring international companies to establish regional headquarters in the kingdom to secure government contracts.

title: November 2022 Patch Tuesday | Microsoft Releases 65 New Vulnerabilities With 10 Critical; Adobe Releases Zero Advisories (for the First Time in Six Years).
summary: In November 2022, Microsoft released 65 new vulnerabilities, with 10 deemed critical, addressing issues like Denial of Service, Elevation of Privilege, and Remote Code Execution. Notably, six zero-day vulnerabilities were fixed, including updates for the Microsoft Exchange ProxyNotShell. For the first time in six years, Adobe released no security advisories, a significant departure from its usual monthly patch schedule.

title: Calamos Investments Launches New Sustainable Equities ETF SROI
summary: Calamos Investments has launched the Calamos Antetokounmpo Global Sustainable Equities ETF (SROI) on NYSE ARCA, in collaboration with NBA star Giannis Antetokounmpo. This actively managed ETF aims for long-term capital appreciation by investing in quality growth companies that integrate ESG principles, utilizing both traditional financial and nonfinancial indicators. The fund will also donate a portion of its profits to charity, reflecting a commitment to community impact.

title: Software company Autodesk lays off 250 employees
summary: Autodesk, a software company, has laid off 250 employees, which is less than 2% of its global workforce. This decision is part of its fiscal year 2024 plans to align resources with key priorities and comes amidst a global economic downturn affecting many tech companies. The affected roles include digital marketing, technical marketing, and web optimization, though the company continues to hire for other key positions.

title: Baidu stock surges after announcement of ChatGPT-style AI bot
