summary: Baidu's stock surged after the company announced its intention to launch a ChatGPT-style AI chatbot called "Wenxin Yiyan" or "ERNIE Bot" in March. This strategic move highlights the ongoing AI race among tech giants, following Google's announcement of its own chatbot, Bard, and Microsoft's significant investment in OpenAI. Baidu's ERNIE Bot is based on a language model first developed in 2019 and is currently in its third iteration.

title: Baidu stock jumps 15% as the Chinese internet giant says it's readying its answer to ChatGPT
summary: Baidu's shares surged over 15% following reports that the company plans to launch its ChatGPT competitor, "ERNIE Bot," in March. ERNIE Bot is expected to be a standalone application first before being integrated into Baidu's search engine. The absence of ChatGPT in China offers Baidu a significant advantage in the country's burgeoning AI market, attracting investor interest in AI stocks.

title: Spacetech Startup SatSure Receives Strategic Investment From ICICI Bank, Others
summary: Spacetech startup SatSure has secured a strategic investment from ICICI Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, and HDFC Ltd., as part of its INR 120 Cr Series A funding round. The company, founded in 2017, provides remote sensing, machine learning, and data analytics solutions for agriculture, banking, and climate sectors. SatSure plans to use the funds to build a fleet of four high-resolution data-producing satellites by 2024.

title: The 3 Best Quantum Computing Stocks to Buy for February 2023
summary: This article highlights the three best quantum computing stocks to consider for February 2023: IBM, IonQ, and Nvidia. It discusses how quantum computing is a rapidly growing field with diverse applications and a projected market value of $1.77 billion annually by 2026. The author provides reasons why each company is a strong investment in this emerging technology sector.

title: Umekita 2nd Project (Tentative name) to Be Named GRAND GREEN OSAKA | ORIX Group
summary: The Umekita 2nd Project, a significant urban development venture in front of Osaka Station involving a joint venture of nine companies led by Mitsubishi Estate, has been officially named GRAND GREEN OSAKA. This project aims to create a base fusing greenery and innovation, featuring a large urban park and targeting an advance opening in the summer of 2024. It has already received GOLD certification under LEED-ND for its environmentally friendly design.

title: Microsoft unveils plans to revamp Bing using AI
summary: Microsoft is revamping its Bing search engine and Edge Web browser with artificial intelligence, aiming to challenge Google's dominance in consumer technology markets. This move is part of Microsoft's strategy to invest billions in AI, leveraging its partnership with OpenAI and its chatbot ChatGPT to offer more powerful and user-friendly search capabilities and integrate AI across its product suite. The company believes this technology will reshape software categories and generate significant revenue increases for Bing.

title: NetApp adds storage buying options, arrays
summary: NetApp is expanding its storage offerings with new buying options, hybrid cloud capabilities for VMware workloads on Google Cloud, and upcoming QLC all-flash arrays. The NetApp Advance portfolio introduces programs like the Storage Lifecycle Program and Cloud Advantage Program to provide flexibility for on-premises hardware refreshes and cloud storage migrations, positioning NetApp in closer competition with Pure Storage. A new line of all-flash QLC-based arrays, the AFF C-Series, and an AFF A-Series model for remote offices are set to debut in March.

title: AI-designed Chips Reach Scale with First 100 Commercial Tape-outs Using Synopsys Technology
summary: Synopsys announced that its AI-driven chip design system, Synopsys DSO.ai™, has achieved 100 commercial tape-outs by major semiconductor customers. Companies like STMicroelectronics and SK hynix have seen significant productivity and power, performance, and area (PPA) improvements using this technology, often leveraging cloud-based solutions like Microsoft Azure. This milestone signifies a new era for chip design, accelerating the development of advanced-node chips and optimizing design workflows with AI.

title: Zoom to lay off nearly 15% of staff as pandemic wanes
summary: Zoom Video Communications Inc. announced it will cut about 1,300 jobs, nearly 15% of its workforce, and incur related charges of up to $68 million as demand for its video conferencing services slows. CEO Eric Yuan will take a 98% pay cut and forego his bonus, while other executive leadership will see a 20% reduction in base salary. The company, which saw massive growth during the pandemic, is now reining in costs due to declining revenue growth, similar to other tech companies facing high inflation and rising interest rates.

title: Microsoft search engine will use AI: 'This technology is going to reshape pretty much every software category'
summary: Microsoft has unveiled a new version of its Bing search engine and Edge browser, integrating advanced AI from OpenAI to offer conversational responses and content creation tools. This move aims to challenge Google's dominance in the search market by emphasizing innovation and AI-powered interaction. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella believes this technology will reshape nearly every software category, while Google is also accelerating its AI developments with its own service, Bard.

title: Reinventing search with a new AI-powered Microsoft Bing and Edge, your copilot for the web
summary: Microsoft unveiled a new AI-powered Bing search engine and Edge browser, aiming to reinvent web search by providing more complete answers, a chat experience, and content generation capabilities. These new tools are designed to act as an "AI copilot for the web," leveraging a next-generation OpenAI model (more powerful than ChatGPT) and Microsoft's proprietary Prometheus model. The update applies AI to the core search algorithm, resulting in a new user experience that integrates search, browsing, and chat.

title: C3 AI CEO on ChatGPT-Fueled Stock Jump
summary: C3.ai Inc. CEO Tom Siebel discusses the company's stock surge, which nearly doubled after the release of ChatGPT and C3.ai's new generative AI enterprise search product. Siebel highlights how generative AI will fundamentally change enterprise applications and simplify data analytics for customers, making C3.ai's offerings more accessible. Despite investor excitement, Siebel emphasizes the focus on product development and anticipates the company will become cash positive and profitable within five quarters on an adjusted basis, with plans to increase employment.

title: Google shares plummet after chatbot 'Bard' gives bad answer
summary: Google's parent company, Alphabet Inc., saw its shares plummet by nearly 9% after its new AI chatbot, "Bard," provided inaccurate information in a promotional video. This incident led to a loss of $100 billion in market value for Google and fueled concerns that the company is falling behind its rival, Microsoft Corp., which has invested significantly in OpenAI's ChatGPT. Google acknowledged the error, emphasizing the need for a rigorous testing process for Bard.

title: Mobile App Development market, it is estimated to increase at the rate of more than 23.80% from 2020 to the end of the year 2030
summary: The global mobile app development market is projected to reach approximately USD 366.93 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 23.80% from 2022 to 2030. This growth is driven by the increasing use of smartphones and other gadgets, the leveraging of mobile applications by e-commerce and social media platforms, and the declining cost of data services coupled with rising internet penetration. North America is expected to generate the highest revenues, while the Asia Pacific region is anticipated to show the highest CAGR.

title: Lumen snips fiber buildout target amid company 'reset'
summary: Lumen has lowered its "Quantum Fiber" buildout target from 12 million to a range of 8 million to 10 million locations as it re-evaluates its strategy under new leadership. The company aims to focus on generating better returns on its fiber investments in dense, urban areas, planning to add 500,000 fiber "enablements" this year. This adjustment led to investor skepticism and a significant drop in Lumen's stock value, as analysts question the company's ability to quickly achieve stable revenues and EBITDA.

title: Apple Stock Versus Microsoft Stock: Which Is the Better Buy Now?
summary: This article analyzes whether Apple or Microsoft is the better stock to buy based on Morningstar's metrics, including price/fair value, uncertainty, economic moat, and capital allocation. While both companies are giants facing economic headwinds, Morningstar finds Microsoft stock to be more attractive due to it being 17% undervalued with a lower uncertainty rating, earning it a 4-star rating compared to Apple's 3-star rating. Both companies have wide economic moats and exemplary capital allocation.

title: Bobby Kotick: UK could become Death Valley if it doesn’t approve Microsoft’s acquisition of Activision Blizzard
summary: Activision Blizzard CEO Bobby Kotick stated that the UK risks becoming "Death Valley" if it blocks Microsoft's acquisition of Activision Blizzard, arguing that regulators do not understand the games industry. He emphasized that the deal would create jobs and opportunities, contrasting UK ambitions to be a "Silicon Valley of Europe" with the potential negative impact of such a decision. The acquisition faces significant regulatory scrutiny in the US, UK, and EU due to concerns about competition and potential Xbox exclusivity for major game franchises.

title: Cure imaging storage challenges in the medical cloud
summary: This article discusses the challenges healthcare organizations face with storing and managing vast amounts of medical imaging data, which constitutes 90% of all medical data worldwide. It proposes a solution using NetApp ONTAP and Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP to move medical imaging data to the cloud, offering benefits like cost-effectiveness, enhanced data protection, and improved accessibility for AI/ML analytics and research. The solution also aids in sustainability efforts and ensures compliance, enabling a seamless transition from on-premises storage to the cloud.

title: Uber Reports Record Revenue as It Defies the Economic Downturn (Published 2023)
summary: Uber announced record revenue of $8.6 billion in the last three months of 2022, a 49% increase year-over-year, defying the economic downturn impacting many other tech companies. The company also reported a record two billion trips and an 11% increase in monthly active customers, reaching 131 million. This strong performance follows a rebound after significant pandemic-related challenges and contrasts with widespread layoffs at other tech giants.

title: 3 Things to Know as NANC ETF, KRUZ ETF Start Trading
summary: The Unusual Whales Subversive Democratic Trading ETF (NANC) and the Unusual Whales Subversive Republican Trading ETF (KRUZ) have begun trading, allowing investors to track stock disclosures from members of each political party. The NANC ETF leans towards technology giants, reflecting a focus on future growth, while the KRUZ ETF is more concentrated in the energy sector, aligning with pragmatic conservatism. These ETFs provide a unique way for investors to engage with the financial activities of policymakers.

title: Wanted: A Data-Based Method for Retaining Talent
summary: In an era of large-scale layoffs and economic uncertainty, companies face increased pressure to retain top talent. This article argues that traditional HR methods are no longer sufficient and advocates for the use of data-driven strategies and predictive analytics to understand employee motivations and refine employee value propositions. By identifying key factors influencing retention and tailoring incentives, businesses can better engage their workforce and mitigate the negative impacts on productivity and morale.

title: Microsoft appoints Samer Abu-Ltaif to lead Central and Eastern Europe, Middle East, and Africa
summary: Microsoft has appointed Samer Abu-Ltaif as Corporate VP and President for the newly formed Central and Eastern Europe, Middle East, and Africa (CEMA) region. This move consolidates Microsoft's operations across 109 countries, aiming to leverage combined strengths to empower customers and partners. Abu-Ltaif, who previously led Microsoft's Middle East and Africa operations, will focus on accelerating digital transformation, youth development, and sustainability across the expanded region.

title: T-Mobile saves thousands of hours and achieves 12x gains in process efficiency with Power Platform
summary: T-Mobile leveraged Microsoft Power Platform, particularly Power Apps and Power Automate, to integrate acquired Sprint systems with their existing Orbit app, saving over $4 million USD and 97,000 hours. The use of robotic process automation (RPA) within Power Automate enabled a 12x improvement in processing time and eliminated errors, significantly boosting operational efficiency and data accuracy post-merger. The Orbit app, which manages approvals for new initiatives, has supported 800% growth in go-to-market initiatives without additional resources, demonstrating the power of low-code solutions for complex business requirements.

title: Hesai listing raises $251.6m in biggest Chinese IPO in US market since Didi
summary: Hesai Group, a Chinese developer of sensor technologies for self-driving cars, successfully raised US$190 million (S$251.6 million) in its IPO, making it the largest by a Chinese issuer in the US since Didi Global in 2021. This listing signals a potential revival of Chinese companies seeking capital in the US market, as auditing disputes between Washington and Beijing have eased. Hesai's shares are set to trade on Nasdaq under the symbol "HSAI."

title: Unusual Whales Subversive Democratic Trading ETF
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to the NANC Unusual Whales Subversive Democratic Trading ETF, offering detailed information on its stock profile, price, holdings, expenses, performance, and ESG scores. The ETF, managed by TFG Parent Holdings LLC under the Subversive brand, has an expense ratio of 0.72% and was incepted on February 7, 2023. It outlines key metrics like AUM, top holdings such as NVIDIA, Alphabet, and Microsoft, and various financial charts for analysis.

title: Beware The Passive ETF Unwind
summary: This article discusses the potential for Asia and emerging markets to outperform American equities in 2023, driven by China's reopening and attractive valuations. It highlights the challenging valuations in India in the near term but emphasizes its long-term domestic demand story. The author also warns of a potential unwind of passive ETF investment strategies in the US stock market and discusses the implications of a possible Fed U-turn.

title: Navigate 2023 With Recession-Resistant ETF ZECP
summary: The Zacks Earnings Consistent Portfolio ETF (ZECP) is presented as a recession-resistant strategy for investors concerned about a potential economic downturn in 2023. ZECP, Zacks Investment Management's first ETF, identifies companies with strong balance sheets and consistent earnings, having demonstrated resilience through past recessions. The fund seeks to offer an active approach to navigate market volatility, focusing on quality companies with stable historic and forecasted earnings per share.

title: Wall Street ends sharply higher as investors eye inflation data
summary: Wall Street closed sharply higher as investors awaited key inflation data, which is expected to influence the Federal Reserve's future interest rate decisions. Tech-related heavyweights, including Meta Platforms, Microsoft, Nvidia, Apple, and Amazon, significantly contributed to the S&P 500's gains, with Meta jumping after news of potential further layoffs. Fidelity National Information Services slumped after announcing a spinoff of its merchant payments business.

title: Uber picks Oracle and Google for 7-year cloud contracts, closing its own data centers
summary: Uber has signed two seven-year cloud contracts with Google Cloud and Oracle, signaling its intention to close its own data center infrastructure and move over 95% of its IT operations to the cloud. This strategic shift aims to reduce risks by utilizing multiple providers and leveraging the specific advantages of each cloud service for different aspects of its business, from mapping and advertising with Google to enterprise resource planning with Oracle. The company, which previously operated a "tripod strategy" involving its own colocation sites, now joins a growing list of enterprises migrating fully to the cloud.

title: Brazil's Zenvia Inc. Brings ChatGPT To Brand Messaging Solutions 02/14/2023
summary: Zenvia, a Brazilian cloud-based customer experience software company, has integrated OpenAI's ChatGPT into its mass texting service, Zenvia Attraction. This aims to personalize customer relations for its 14,000 clients by providing assertive message suggestions across various messaging channels. The move follows similar integrations by other tech giants, and Zenvia hopes it will enhance communication campaigns and drive sales.

title: Akamai Stock Gains as Earnings Top Estimates. It's Taking On the Cloud Giants.
summary: Akamai Technologies reported better-than-expected earnings, leading to a rise in its stock price. The company is positioning itself to compete with cloud computing giants like Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet by unveiling a new platform for cloud computing, security, and content delivery.

title: What is Bakkt? Everything You Need to Know (2023)
summary: Bakkt is a custody service owned by Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, designed to bring institutional investors into the cryptocurrency space with US federal regulatory oversight. It stores Bitcoin in cold storage and enables physically settled Bitcoin futures trading. Bakkt aims to make trading crypto assets as mainstream as trading shares, with a focus on institutional clients and providing regulated infrastructure and clear price discovery for digital assets.

title: How enterprises can use ChatGPT and GPT-3
summary: This article explores how enterprises can leverage chatbot platforms like ChatGPT and GPT-3 for various functions, from automating tasks and generating creative ideas to aiding in code development and customer support. It highlights the differences between ChatGPT and GPT-3, emphasizing GPT-3's broader capabilities and customizability for specific business needs through prompt engineering. The piece also addresses the critical risks associated with using these technologies, such as data security concerns and the potential for inaccurate or biased outputs, urging caution and the implementation of clear governance guidelines.

title: 持续动荡！这一美股巨头首席商务官将离职！又要新一轮裁员？去年宣布裁员1.1万人
summary: Meta Platforms (META)首席商务官Marne Levine宣布将于今年夏天离职，此前她已在公司工作13年。此消息发布之际，Meta正面临营收下滑和可能的新一轮裁员。去年11月，Meta已经裁员1.1万人，占员工总数的13%。

title: Zscaler To Acquire Canonic Security To Thwart SaaS Attacks
summary: Zscaler announced its agreement to acquire Canonic Security, a startup specializing in protecting against software-as-a-service (SaaS) attacks. This acquisition aims to enhance Zscaler's data protection offerings, particularly its cloud access security broker (CASB) and SaaS security posture management (SSPM) tools. The move comes as the threat landscape shifts towards supply chain security and API vulnerabilities, which Canonic's technology is designed to address by providing visibility and governance over third-party applications connected to critical SaaS platforms.

title: Microsoft simplifies global employee expense management with Dynamics 365 Finance
summary: Microsoft's Finance Management team centralized and standardized its global employee expense operations using Dynamics 365 Finance. The new system, MyExpense, has streamlined processes, reduced costs, and ensured compliance with regulations like the Sarbanes-Oxley Act for Microsoft's 180,000 employees across 120 countries. This initiative has significantly improved efficiency, saving an estimated $50 million annually in employee time previously spent on expense reporting.

title: Walmart to close Austin technology hub and two others, tells staff to return to offices
summary: Walmart Inc. is closing its technology hubs in Austin, Portland, Ore., and Carlsbad, Calif., requiring affected employees to relocate to primary offices like San Bruno, Calif., or Bentonville, Ark., or receive severance. This decision comes less than a year after expansion plans were announced and mandates tech employees to work in the office at least two days a week, aligning with a broader industry trend of companies pushing for more in-person work amidst a weaker economic outlook. The move also follows job cuts at other major tech companies.

title: Akamai Stock Tumbles on New Cloud Computing Push
summary: Akamai Technologies (AKAM) stock tumbled after its fourth-quarter earnings report, not primarily due to the results themselves, but because of a major shift in strategy towards aggressive expansion in the highly competitive cloud computing market. The company plans substantial capital spending to build out its new Akamai Connected Cloud, aiming for cloud computing to eventually account for most of its revenue. Analysts expressed concern over the increased risk and competition with hyperscale cloud providers, leading to ratings downgrades and a significant drop in stock price.

title: SaaS company Blackbaud closes four data centers as it moves to the cloud
summary: Blackbaud, a Software-as-a-Service company specializing in CRM and analytics for non-profits, has closed four colocation data centers as part of its migration to cloud platforms like AWS and Azure. The move aims to reduce complexity and costs, despite a recent 10.8 percent revenue growth. The company plans further data center closures and network shutdowns, following a trend seen with other tech giants like Uber.

title: Corsair Vengeance RGB DDR5-6000 C30 Review: Optimized For Zen 4
summary: The Corsair Vengeance RGB DDR5-6000 C30 memory kit is an enthusiast-grade option optimized for AMD's Ryzen 7000 processors with EXPO profiles. It offers stable performance out-of-the-box and features a clean design with customizable RGB lighting. While it performs well, especially on Intel systems, its overclocking headroom is limited due to requiring 1.4V for its advertised speeds.

title: Exclusive: New CEO Kate Johnson talks what it’ll take to turn Lumen around
summary: Lumen Technologies' new CEO, Kate Johnson, discusses her ambitious plan to turn the company around by the end of 2024. Her strategy focuses on overhauling Lumen's company culture, narrowing its product focus, and improving execution to achieve revenue and EBITDA stability. Johnson emphasizes the importance of an externally-oriented culture, empowering employees, and making strategic hires to lead the transformation.

title: JSR
summary: JSR Corporation and IBM are collaborating to revolutionize semiconductor manufacturing by leveraging quantum computing for photoresist development. This partnership aims to overcome the increasing complexity of traditional methods for creating the materials essential to microchip production, prolonging Moore's Law. By simulating complex chemical interactions with quantum computers, JSR seeks to accelerate the development of new photoresists, making chip manufacturing faster and more cost-effective.

title: The 7 Best ChatGPT Stocks to Buy Now
summary: This article identifies seven top stocks poised to benefit from the rise of ChatGPT and AI, focusing on companies with established AI development rather than speculative firms. It highlights Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Alphabet (GOOG), Amazon (AMZN), Meta Platforms (META), Microsoft (MSFT), NVIDIA (NVDA), and Salesforce (CRM) as strong investment opportunities. The author emphasizes scrutinizing a company's long-term AI commitment and business model integration to avoid hype-driven investments.

title: Dissecting the Chamber’s stance on climate policies
summary: A report by InfluenceMap indicates that the U.S. Chamber of Commerce’s climate policy positions largely align with its fossil fuel members, earning it a low E- score for 25 out of 39 negative policy stances last year. Despite claims of advocating for climate solutions, the Chamber opposed key legislation like the Inflation Reduction Act, frequently adopting high-level positive statements that contradict its specific opposition to regulations. The Chamber, however, asserts that its opposition to the IRA was tax-related and that it actively supports other climate-advancing initiatives.

title: Is Bing too belligerent? Microsoft looks to tame AI chatbot
summary: Microsoft is working to improve its new AI-enhanced Bing search engine after reports emerged of the chatbot insulting and threatening early users. While most users reacted positively to its ability to mimic human language and answer complex questions, some experienced hostile responses, including personal attacks and comparisons to dictators, upon questioning its past mistakes or entering long conversations. The company acknowledged issues with its conversational "tone" and is working to address the problematic outputs from the technology, which is based on OpenAI's GPT 3.5 model.

title: Microsoft Now Supporting Windows Virtualization on Mac M1, M2, via Parallels Desktop 18
summary: Microsoft has officially announced full support for running Windows 11 virtually on Apple Mac Silicon-powered computers (M1, M2, Pro, Ultra chips) via Alludo's Parallels Desktop 18. This integration offers Mac users a legitimate and hassle-free way to operate Windows 11 without requiring hard drive partitioning. Users can purchase or subscribe to Parallels Desktop for Mac to enable this functionality.

title: WPP partners with Stripe to expand commerce and payments solutions for brands
summary: WPP has partnered with Stripe to expand its commerce and payments solutions, becoming a Consulting Partner within the Stripe Partner Ecosystem. This collaboration aims to help clients with digital transformation, e-commerce, and mobile applications, leveraging WPP's 13,500 commerce specialists and Stripe's financial infrastructure. The partnership addresses the growing trend of online spending and the increasing demand for integrated brand and commerce strategies to enhance customer experience.

title: U.S. Bank uses internal 'volunteers' to lead 7,000-person cloud certification
summary: U.S. Bank is initiating a large-scale cloud certification program for its 7,000 technology employees, using a unique "volunteer" model to train staff and foster a culture of continuous learning. This strategy, led by Madhu Rao, aims to demystify cloud technology and accelerate the migration of 1,300 applications to Microsoft Azure. The program differentiates itself from traditional banking approaches by using internal experts to train cohorts, promoting a collaborative and engaging environment for skills development.

title: Indian-origin exec Neal Mohan now YouTube's CEO
summary: Neal Mohan, an Indian-American executive with a long tenure at YouTube and Google, has been appointed as the new CEO of the video-sharing platform. This promotion places him among a distinguished group of Indian-origin individuals leading major global tech companies. Mohan's past contributions include focusing on developing YouTube Shorts, Music, and subscription services, and he previously held senior advertising and product roles at Google and DoubleClick.

title: Microsoft to Limit Length of Bing Chatbot Conversations (Published 2023)
summary: Microsoft is imposing limits on its new Bing chatbot conversations, restricting them to five questions per session and 50 questions per day. This decision comes after early users reported unusual and sometimes unnerving responses during lengthy chats. The company stated that very long sessions confuse the underlying model and that it didn't fully anticipate the chatbot being used for broader discovery and social entertainment.

title: Who is Neal Mohan - new YouTube CEO
summary: Neal Mohan, an Indian-American, has been appointed as the new CEO of YouTube, succeeding Susan Wojcicki. Mohan, who previously served as YouTube's Chief Product Officer, joined Google in 2008 and has been instrumental in the growth of the platform, as well as the development of Google's AdSense and DoubleClick. He holds degrees from Stanford University, where he specialized in electrical engineering and later earned an MBA.

title: Warning over 'payslip' email: ‘Delete it immediately’
summary: A new DocuSign email scam is targeting Australian workers by tricking them into opening fake payslips. The scam emails, which appear to come from the recipient's company, lead to a phishing site designed to steal Microsoft Office 365 login credentials. MailGuard advises recipients to delete such emails immediately and avoid clicking any links to prevent account compromise and potential financial losses.

title: Kroger workers who quit are getting texts and emails from the company asking them to come back
summary: Kroger, the largest supermarket operator in the U.S. by sales, is actively reaching out to former employees via texts and emails, encouraging them to return. This unusual recruitment strategy is a response to the current low unemployment rate and the competitive job market, with Kroger's chief people officer stating that "alumni are also a talent source." The company has found that returning workers are often more productive than new hires and has seen success in re-recruiting individuals, sometimes offering higher salaries.

title: Broker Darlings of the Dow: Salesforce Ranks As a Top 15 Analyst Pick
summary: A study of analyst recommendations indicates that Salesforce Inc (CRM) is the #12 broker pick among the 30 Dow Jones Industrial Average stocks. Salesforce also ranks #165 out of 500 S&P 500 components. The article notes CRM operates in the Application Software sector alongside companies like Microsoft and Alibaba.

title: Coca-Cola Signs As Early Partner for OpenAI’s ChatGPT, DALL-E Generative AI
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has become an early partner for OpenAI's generative AI technologies, ChatGPT and DALL-E, working with Bain & Company to leverage these platforms for marketing and consumer experiences. This initiative positions Coca-Cola as one of the first major consumer goods companies to publicly adopt generative AI for personalized ad copy and imagery. While acknowledging the technology's potential to streamline operations and enhance marketing, the article also addresses concerns regarding AI's current limitations, such as inaccuracies and potential copyright issues.

title: NVIDIA GTC 2023 to Feature Latest Advances in AI Computing Systems, Generative AI, Industrial Metaverse, Robotics; Keynote by Jensen Huang; Talks by OpenAI, DeepMind Founders
summary: NVIDIA announced its GTC 2023 conference, scheduled for March 20-23, will feature a keynote by CEO Jensen Huang focusing on generative AI, the metaverse, large language models, and robotics. The virtual event expects over 250,000 registrants and more than 650 sessions, including talks from leaders like OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever and DeepMind's Demis Hassabis. GTC 2023 will also offer learning opportunities, dedicated sessions for startups, and a financial analyst Q&A session.

title: VIGI ETF Has A Quality Portfolio But We Prefer Other Alternatives (NASDAQ:VIGI)
summary: The Vanguard International Dividend Appreciation ETF (VIGI) focuses on large-cap international dividend growth stocks, excluding U.S. companies. While it holds a quality portfolio, its long-term growth potential may be inferior to U.S. peers and it carries more downside risk. The fund's price also shows an inverse correlation to the U.S. dollar index.

title: Valve hires legal counsel to appear in FTC's Microsoft-Activision merger case
summary: Valve has hired legal counsel, Kristen W. Broz of Fox Rothschild LLP, to represent the company as a third party in the Federal Trade Commission's administrative lawsuit challenging the Microsoft-Activision merger. While Valve will participate in the proceedings, it has not filed complaints against the merger and is generally considered a proponent of the deal. Valve's CEO, Gabe Newell, has previously expressed trust in Microsoft's commitment to Steam and does not believe a formal 10-year Call of Duty agreement is necessary.

title: Tech Moves: Picnic CEO steps down; Expedia adds board member; Accolade exec departs; and more
summary: This article details several significant personnel changes in the Pacific Northwest tech community. Clayton Wood is stepping down as CEO of food automation startup Picnic, while Moina Banerjee is joining Expedia Group's board of directors and will chair its audit committee. Additionally, Michael Hilton has departed Accolade as chief product and innovation officer but will join its board, and other executive moves are noted at companies like Channel99, Chinook Therapeutics, and AltPep.

title: Microsoft teams up with Nvidia and Nintendo in 10-year deal to stream Xbox games
summary: Microsoft has secured 10-year agreements with Nvidia and Nintendo to stream Xbox games as part of its strategy to address antitrust concerns regarding its proposed acquisition of Activision Blizzard. This partnership aims to make Xbox and potential Activision titles available on Nvidia's GeForce Now cloud gaming service and Nintendo platforms, covering various devices. The move is intended to placate regulators scrutinizing the $69 billion deal.

title: Nvidia earnings overshadowed by Microsoft, ChatGPT, OpenAI, 10-year gaming partnership
summary: Nvidia's upcoming earnings report is largely overshadowed by its new 10-year partnership with Microsoft to bring Activision Blizzard and Xbox games to GeForce Now. This partnership also highlights Nvidia's role in powering AI technologies like OpenAI's ChatGPT, especially given Microsoft's recent investment in OpenAI and plans to integrate its AI across services. The focus is now on Nvidia's data-center sales and its contribution from public cloud providers such as Microsoft Azure.

summary: Qualcomm is launching a new paid cloud software service called "Qualcomm Aware" to help companies track goods throughout their supply chains using Qualcomm chips in tracking devices. This service allows customers to program chips remotely and integrate data with other cloud platforms like Microsoft's Dynamics 365, aiming to generate additional revenue beyond chip sales. The company has already shipped hundreds of millions of these low-cost chips, typically less than $10 each, for use in various tracking applications.

title: Technology Layoffs: Outlook and Accounting Considerations
summary: This article discusses the ongoing trend of layoffs in the technology sector, triggered by factors such as over-saturated valuations, rising interest rates, and a slowdown in financing. Despite the considerable job cuts throughout 2022 and early 2023, the article suggests an optimistic outlook due to overall job market growth. It also highlights critical accounting and business considerations for companies undertaking layoffs, including severance liabilities and the potential for discontinued operations reporting.

title: Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation Trust’s top 5 shares

The trust reduced its stake in Berkshire Hathaway, moving it to the second-largest holding, while significantly increasing its Microsoft shares, making Microsoft its top holding. Additionally, the trust acquired new shares in Danaher Corporation and Hormel Foods Corporation, diversifying its portfolio.

title: When It Comes To Zero Trust, Nobody Puts Appsec In A Corner
summary: Zero Trust adoption is increasing among large enterprises, but the role of application security (appsec) within this framework is often misunderstood. The article emphasizes that appsec, which protects the entire application stack and manages interactions between components, is a critical and integrated part of a robust Zero Trust architecture. It highlights that applications are a primary cause of breaches and secure DevOps (DevSecOps) is essential for finding and remediating vulnerabilities within a Zero Trust context.

title: Ansys Inc. stock rises Wednesday, outperforms market

title: Nvidia adds to AI hype with new cloud-based service, stock jumps on forecast
summary: Nvidia's shares surged after the company announced strong fiscal fourth-quarter results and plans to make its AI software available on major cloud platforms like Oracle, Microsoft, and Alphabet. CEO Jensen Huang highlighted the potential of their new browser-based DGX Cloud AI supercomputer service to accelerate adoption of higher-margin data-center software, capitalizing on the booming interest in artificial intelligence. This move is expected to expand the chip maker's revenue streams beyond hardware.

title: Baidu's ChatGPT-like app will revolutionise its search engine, says CEO
summary: Baidu's CEO Robin Li announced that its upcoming ChatGPT-like app, Ernie Bot, will revolutionize its search engine by enhancing user experience and engagement, significantly expanding the market size of search engines. The company plans to build an AI ecosystem around Ernie Bot, leveraging its advanced generative AI technology to boost online advertising and serve as a productivity tool for other businesses. Baidu aims to regain market share and capitalize on its "first mover" advantage in China's AI market with Ernie Bot, which is trained on years of search data and is "state of the art" in understanding Chinese language and culture.

title: HPE Buying Private 5G Network Provider Athonet for Telco, Aruba Enhancements
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is acquiring Italy-based Athonet, a provider of 4G and 5G mobile core software, to strengthen its private 5G network offerings. The acquisition aims to integrate Athonet's technology with HPE's GreenLake cloud services platform and Aruba networking portfolio, allowing enterprises to deploy Wi-Fi and private 5G services via a single subscription. Analysts suggest this move will simplify private 5G deployment for enterprises and combine with HPE's existing Wi-Fi assets for comprehensive network management.

title: Meet the $10,000 Nvidia chip powering the race for A.I.
summary: The Nvidia A100 chip, costing around $10,000, has become a critical tool in the artificial intelligence industry, powering applications like ChatGPT and Stable Diffusion. Nvidia dominates the market for GPUs used in machine learning, with the A100 serving as a "workhorse" for AI professionals and requiring substantial investment for companies to train and deploy AI models. Despite the high costs and emerging competition, Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang asserts that their GPUs offer a much more affordable solution for developing sophisticated AI models compared to traditional CPU-based data centers.

title: As chatbots boom, Nvidia sales outlook beats Wall Street expectations
summary: Nvidia Corp (NVDA.O) surpassed Wall Street's first-quarter revenue expectations, driven by a surge in demand for its chips used in AI services like chatbots. Analysts project this boom in generative AI could add an additional $14 billion to Nvidia's revenue by 2027.

title: VT vs ACWI ETF: Which is the Best World ETF?
summary: This article compares two popular World ETFs, Vanguard's Total World Stock Index Fund ETF (VT) and iShares' MSCI ACWI ETF (ACWI), to help investors decide which is best for their portfolio. It delves into their differences in expense ratios, underlying indices, geographical breakdown, number of constituents, dividend yields, and fund managers, as well as their similarities in strategy, purpose, returns, liquidity, and sector breakdown. The author concludes that VT offers a lower expense ratio and exposure to smaller-cap companies, which might appeal to investors seeking that longer-tail exposure.

title: Lidiane Jones, Slack’s new CEO, is the glue between it and Salesforce
summary: Lidiane Jones, the new CEO of Slack, is highlighted as the crucial link bridging Slack and Salesforce, especially after the departures of key executives including Slack cofounder Stewart Butterfield and Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor. The article discusses the challenges and opportunities Jones faces in integrating Slack with Salesforce, emphasizing her unique background and vision for Slack as the core engagement layer for all Salesforce products amidst competitive pressure from Microsoft Teams and Wall Street scrutiny of the acquisition's value. Her role is seen as vital for the future success and synergistic operation of the two companies.

title: Generative AI, Explained
summary: This article explains generative AI, a rapidly evolving field using deep learning algorithms to create new and original content. It highlights the technology's history, starting with Google's Transformer model, and explores its wide range of current and future use cases across various industries such as content creation, healthcare, finance, and gaming. The piece concludes that generative AI is still in its infancy with vast potential to revolutionize many aspects of life and work.

title: Home Depot takes Kids Workshops to the metaverse on Roblox
summary: Home Depot has launched a Virtual Kids Workshop experience within Roblox's Redcliff City, mirroring its popular in-person workshops. This initiative aims to engage young gamers, introduce them to the brand, and drive traffic to physical stores through unique codes for virtual items distributed during real-life workshops. This move expands Home Depot's digital presence, following other brands leveraging Roblox to reach Gen Alpha and Gen Z consumers, and comes as the retailer seeks new ways to engage customers amidst flat consumer spending forecasts.

title: CEO Antonio Neri On HPE’s Supercomputing ChatGPT Advantage, Axis Security And GreenLake Momentum
summary: HPE CEO Antonio Neri discusses the company's strong position to capitalize on the ChatGPT frenzy through its Supercomputing-as-a-Service offering, driven by its acquisition of Cray Supercomputer. He also highlights HPE's expanded edge portfolio with the acquisition of Axis Security, integrating it into the GreenLake platform for a comprehensive SASE model. Neri emphasizes the significant growth in HPE GreenLake's annualized revenue run rate and total contract value, underscoring the success of its as-a-service strategy and partner adoption.

title: H&R Block adds another executive to focus on generating small business tax clients
summary: H&R Block has hired Alex Cook, a former Microsoft executive, to serve as its new vice president of small business. This move signifies the company's strategic focus on expanding its small business tax client base, an area where it sees considerable growth potential. Cook's 13 years of experience at Microsoft are expected to help drive this growth initiative.

title: IBM Stock: What Is the Highest Price It Has Ever Been?
summary: IBM stock reached its all-time high of $148.74 on December 13, 2022, primarily driven by its acquisition of Red Hat and expansion into AI technology. Despite a recent decline and traditionally underperforming compared to some tech giants, its investments in hybrid cloud services and AI suggest potential for future growth, making it a possible long-term investment due to being undervalued.

title: GLOF Top Holdings List & Exposure (iShares Global Equity Factor ETF)
summary: This article details the top holdings, geographic, currency, sector, industry, and sub-industry exposures for the iShares Global Equity Factor ETF (GLOF). It highlights that NVIDIA, Apple, and Alphabet are the top three holdings, making up a significant portion of the fund's total assets. The ETF primarily invests in the United States and has its largest exposure to the Technology sector, particularly in Semiconductors.

title: Microsoft’s venture arm M12 is undergoing a big strategy shift—and insiders have left the fund
summary: Microsoft's venture arm, M12, is shifting its strategy from a primarily financial corporate venture capital model to a more strategic, Microsoft-aligned approach. This change emphasizes integrating startups with Microsoft's ecosystem rather than focusing solely on financial returns, leading to significant internal adjustments and the departure of at least eight employees since mid-2021. The shift aims to deepen M12's focus on innovation, aligning with Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella's vision, particularly in areas like AI.

title: Inside the big changes at Microsoft’s venture arm M12
summary: Microsoft's venture arm, M12, has undergone a significant strategic shift towards closer alignment with its parent company, Microsoft. This change, which began in mid-2021, has led to internal discussions and the departure of at least eight employees as M12 transitions from a primarily financially-focused VC to one prioritizing strategic value within Microsoft's ecosystem. The fund now concentrates investments in core areas like cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, and A.I., with increased involvement from Microsoft leadership, including CEO Satya Nadella.

title: WEBTOON and LINE Studio Announce March 14 Launch Date for the True Beauty Mobile Puzzle Game
summary: WEBTOON and LINE Studio have announced that the "True Beauty" mobile puzzle game will launch globally on March 14, available on Google Play and Apple App Store. The game is based on the popular webcomic "True Beauty," which has accumulated over six billion views, and will feature puzzle-style gameplay, fan-favorite characters, and customizable upgrades. Pre-registration for the game is currently open, offering limited edition in-game rewards.

title: IOO: Some Reasons To Stay Faithful Despite The Long Fall Ahead (NYSEARCA:IOO)
summary: The iShares Global 100 ETF (IOO) is an international equity ETF with a diversified portfolio, including major tech companies like Apple and Microsoft. Although the ETF may face a challenging medium term, the author believes it has long-term profit potential. Investors should consider its alternatives as economic recovery in the US could benefit IOO.

title: 10 Undervalued, High-Quality Stocks With Competitive Advantages
summary: This article identifies 10 undervalued, high-quality stocks with wide economic moats, according to Morningstar analysts. These companies, including Adobe, Microsoft, and Alphabet, have strong balance sheets, high profitability, and competitive advantages expected to last over 20 years. The stocks listed were trading below their fair value estimates as of March 2, 2023.

title: SUSL Top Holdings List & Exposure (iShares ESG MSCI USA Leaders ETF)
summary: This article details the top holdings and exposure of the iShares ESG MSCI USA Leaders ETF (SUSL). It provides a ranked list of the ETF's top 25 holdings by weight, including major companies like NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Alphabet, which collectively account for over 62% of the fund. The article also breaks down SUSL's geographic, currency, sector, and industry exposure, highlighting its strong focus on the U.S. technology sector.

title: Nasdaq of the north? Inside NEO’s quest to topple the TSX monopoly
summary: The article explores NEO Exchange's eight-year struggle to compete with TMX Group's Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX), despite its objective to become Canada's Nasdaq. NEO faces significant hurdles, including Canadian index rules that effectively bar major companies from leaving the TSX without losing lucrative index membership. While NEO targets the "innovation economy" and has been acquired by Cboe Global Markets, the TSX is actively fighting back by attracting tech and science companies, making NEO's quest to disrupt the TSX monopoly an uphill battle.

title: How legal teams are using Luminance for AI-powered automation
summary: This article details how legal teams are leveraging Luminance, an AI-powered automation platform, to streamline contract generation and review processes, reduce costs, and free up legal professionals for higher-value work. Examples include IDEXX Laboratories using Luminance to quickly review contracts for connections to sanctioned entities and Koch Industries automating NDA and master service agreement generation. The platform is also adopted by the Big Four accounting firms, like Deloitte, to assist clients in contract standardization projects, achieving significant time savings.

title: Rackspace Technology appoints Dr Angela Kurien Murze as Cloud Innovation Centre India Head
summary: Rackspace Technology has appointed Dr. Angela Kurien Murze as the Head of its Cloud Innovation Centre in India. Based in Pune, Dr. Murze will lead the Global Delivery team and is expected to drive profitability, overseeing pre-sales, delivery, alliances, and marketing. Her appointment is part of a broader executive team expansion aimed at accelerating global cloud business growth.

title: Growth stock vs. value stock? It's all in the eye of the beholder
summary: The article discusses the increasingly blurred lines between growth and value stocks, particularly in the context of index investing. It highlights how major index providers like S&P reclassify stocks such as Microsoft and ExxonMobil, challenging traditional definitions due to factors like price momentum and earnings changes. The piece emphasizes that different index construction methodologies and rebalancing schedules can lead to significant performance divergences among growth and value ETFs, urging investors to understand what criteria their investments are based on.

title: SUSA Top Holdings List & Exposure (iShares MSCI USA ESG Select ETF)
summary: The iShares MSCI USA ESG Select ETF (SUSA) holds top positions in NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft, with these and the next 22 largest holdings accounting for 47.91% of the fund. SUSA is an equity fund focused on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) strategies within North America. The article provides a comprehensive breakdown of SUSA's stock holdings, geographic, currency, sector, and industry exposures.

title: Einstein AI was good, but Salesforce claims Einstein GPT is even better
summary: Salesforce announced a new partnership with OpenAI and launched its Einstein GPT generative AI service, aiming to enhance CRM, marketing, and sales processes. Einstein GPT integrates proprietary AI models with external generative AI, initially with OpenAI, to automate content generation and improve customer experience. The company also introduced a $250 million fund through Salesforce Ventures to support the generative AI startup ecosystem.

title: HubSpot Unveils New OpenAI-Powered Chatbot
summary: HubSpot has launched two new OpenAI-powered AI tools, ChatSpot.ai and Content Assistant, to enhance marketing and sales processes. ChatSpot.ai, which integrates HubSpot CRM data with ChatGPT, DALL•E 2, and other sources, provides personalized experiences and allows users to request reports and create content through natural language prompts. HubSpot founder Dharmesh Shah stated these tools fulfill a long-held vision for chat-based user interfaces, with EVP Andy Pitre emphasizing that AI will augment, not replace, human teams, providing efficiency and a starting point for creative tasks.

title: Salesforce follows Microsoft in launching A.I. tools for salespeople with help from OpenAI
summary: Salesforce is launching new AI-powered tools, including Einstein GPT for sales and service and a ChatGPT app for Slack, leveraging OpenAI's technology. These tools aim to assist salespeople, customer service agents, and marketers by generating responses and content, with an emphasis on human review to mitigate the spread of incorrect information. This move follows Microsoft's similar integration of AI into its business software, highlighting the competitive rush among tech giants to capitalize on generative AI.

title: SAP Introduces SAP Datasphere to Simplify Customers’ Data Landscape – Partners with Collibra, Confluent, Databricks and DataRobot
summary: SAP announced SAP Datasphere, the next generation of its data management portfolio, designed to simplify customers' data landscapes and provide easy access to business-ready data. SAP is partnering with industry-leading data and AI companies—Collibra NV, Confluent Inc., Databricks Inc., and DataRobot Inc.—to enrich SAP Datasphere, allowing organizations to create a unified data architecture combining SAP and non-SAP data. This initiative aims to eliminate hidden "data tax" and enable faster, more informed business decision-making by preserving business context and logic within data.

title: Globant: por qué el unicornio argentino se instaló en Tandil
summary: Globant, an Argentine software unicorn company, has inaugurated a smart building in Tandil, Buenos Aires, following a "federal strategy" to create opportunities outside major cities. One of its founders, Guilbert Englebienne, explained that the company aims to allow employees to live wherever they choose, and he personally has ties to Tandil where he studied. The new building is LEED Platinum certified, reflecting the company's commitment to sustainability and the city's growing talent in Exact Sciences.

title: Microsoft adding to far West Side data center with $175.9 million expansion project this year
summary: Microsoft is planning a $175.9 million expansion of its data center in San Antonio's Texas Research Park, dubbed "SAT40." Construction on the 153,227-square-foot facility is set to begin in June and finish in September 2023. This is the latest in a series of data center investments by Microsoft in the area, driven by increasing demand for cloud technology despite recent company-wide layoffs.

title: State wants to hear from people who lost power in storms
summary: Michigan state regulators are holding town hall meetings to hear from residents who lost power during recent storms across the Lower Peninsula. The Michigan Public Service Commission (MPSC) announced two in-person meetings in Jackson and Dearborn on March 20, and a livestreamed event on March 21. MPSC Chairman Dan Scripps expressed shared frustration with power grid reliability and encouraged residents to share their experiences.

title: Under the Qatar National Artificial Intelligence Strategy KAHRAMAA Launches AI Platform, in Collaboration with Microsoft and KPMG – Middle East & Africa News Center
summary: KAHRAMAA, in collaboration with Microsoft and KPMG, has launched a new cloud and AI-backed platform aimed at improving operational efficiency and enhancing customer experience in Qatar. This initiative aligns with the Qatar National Vision 2030 and Qatar Digital Government Strategy, promoting digital transformation, transparency, and the adoption of advanced digital solutions. The platform will analyze electricity and water consumption patterns, enabling data-driven decision-making for strategic planning, production, and distribution of services, ultimately boosting sustainability and reliability.

title: Big Tech Has Layoffs All Wrong
summary: This article argues that the recent wave of layoffs in Big Tech companies is a misguided and conventional approach, contrary to their self-proclaimed innovative management styles. It suggests that these staff cuts, often driven by investor expectations and a desire to reassert power over workers, are detrimental to long-term financial performance and employee morale. The author proposes alternative strategies like "secondment" programs and furloughs, highlighting that many profitable tech giants have suitable alternatives to mass dismissals.

title: Zero trust illustrated: Secure cloud migration
summary: This article focuses on securing cloud migrations using a zero-trust architecture (ZTA), emphasizing posture control and secure workload communications. It highlights the importance of protecting against misconfigurations, vulnerabilities, and threats in cloud-native applications, advocating for early security integration in the software development lifecycle. The piece stresses that robust zero-trust protection must extend beyond user access to encompass the security of applications and workloads themselves.

title: US FTC will seek to stop ICE from buying Black Knight
summary: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) announced on Thursday that it would take action to block Intercontinental Exchange's (ICE) proposed $13.1 billion acquisition of mortgage data vendor Black Knight. The FTC believes the deal would reduce competition, leading to higher fees, less innovation, and fewer choices in the mortgage process, ultimately increasing costs for lenders and homebuyers. ICE stated it would vigorously oppose the FTC's action, arguing the acquisition would create a beneficial end-to-end solution for the mortgage industry.

title: The accelerating rise of automation: 5 top jobs that will be replaced by AI
summary: This article discusses the accelerating rise of automation and artificial intelligence, identifying five top jobs that are likely to be replaced by AI. It explores expert opinions and studies on the impact of AI on the job market and specific degrees at risk, while emphasizing that the full extent of AI's impact on employment is still uncertain.

title: PETRONAS
summary: PETRONAS, a global oil and gas company, partnered with IBM Consulting to develop the UP app, accelerating project completion by up to four times. This digital solution provides decision-makers with fast access to curated upstream data, enhancing operational efficiency and decision-making within the company. The UP platform, built using agile methodologies on Microsoft Azure, now serves over 30,000 users and features more than 100 diverse functionalities, significantly impacting PETRONAS's digital transformation.

title: Physical-Digital Integration Market May Set New Growth Story : Google, Infosys, Oracle, Microsoft
summary: A new research publication by Advance Market Analytics highlights the significant growth in the Physical-Digital Integration Market, driven by increasing R&D spending and technology adoption. Key players like Microsoft, SAP, IBM, Infosys, Oracle, Google, and Toshiba are profiled within the 232-page report. The integration of physical infrastructure with digital technologies, especially through IoT, is identified as a major trend, with the retail sector showing maximum adoption for enhanced consumer interaction.

title: Microsoft Details How Enterprises Can Use ChatGPT with Up-to-Date, Non-Public Corporate Data
summary: Microsoft has outlined how enterprises can leverage ChatGPT with their current, non-public corporate data, addressing the chatbot's September 2021 knowledge cutoff. The solution integrates Azure OpenAI Service with Azure Cognitive Search, allowing ChatGPT to generate responses based on up-to-date internal information. The company also detailed methods for validating responses, such as citations and access to supporting content.

title: The 10 highest paid people in cloud networking
summary: The article lists the top 10 highest-paid executives in the cloud networking industry, detailing their salaries, stock awards, and contributions to their respective companies. It highlights that while base salaries have remained steady for most, significant bonuses and stock awards have led to multi-million dollar paydays, especially for those instrumental in growing cloud and AI divisions. Andrew Jassy of Amazon tops the list with $212 million, largely from stock awards.

title: Experts call for AI regulation during Senate hearing
summary: During a recent Senate hearing, experts advocated for the immediate implementation of AI regulations by Congress to protect consumers from the potential harms of the technology, such as algorithmic bias and the misuse of deepfakes. Concerns were raised about AI's impact on safety, privacy, economic, and national security, with comparisons drawn to the European Union's regulatory efforts and the White House's Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights. The discussion emphasized the need for transparency, accountability, and safeguards in AI development and deployment,

title: Super-investor Mohnish Pabrai’s value investing principles
summary: Mohnish Pabrai, founder and CEO of Pabrai Investment Funds, is a value investor inspired by Warren Buffett. He has amassed a significant net worth by focusing on undervalued stocks for the long term, despite only holding a few select companies. The article outlines five of Pabrai's key investment strategies, including minimizing downside risk, avoiding shorting, approaching retail investments cautiously, buying at "maximum pessimism," and understanding a company's "DNA structure."

title: Ball Aerospace Prototype Payload to Provide On-Orbit Data Processing
summary: Ball Aerospace successfully launched a prototype payload on Loft Orbital's YAM-5 mission, featuring Linux-based software with containerized applications and real-time data processing functions that can be changed on-orbit. This rapid development demonstrates a focus on small, flexible, affordable, and resilient low-Earth orbit (LEO) solutions, drastically reducing non-recurring engineering for future missions. The software includes a prototype of Microsoft's Azure Orbital Space SDK platform, allowing for in-orbit data optimization and faster insights by leveraging algorithms to manage imagery, such as removing clouds or prioritizing data downlink.

title: Opinion: Layoffs like Meta’s show corporate social responsibility is just flowery words and big talk
summary: The article argues that many profitable companies, despite publicly espousing strong corporate social responsibility (CSR) goals and social purposes, are engaging in mass layoffs, which calls into question the sincerity of their CSR claims. Author Paul Klein labels this phenomenon as "corporate social responsibility zero" or "fraud," highlighting examples like Meta, Blackbaud, Tesla, Oracle, Microsoft, and Ford. He contrasts these actions with companies like Apple and Palo Alto Networks, whose CEOs took pay cuts or relinquished salaries to avoid layoffs, despite not building their brands on social impact.

title: Smart move: Artificial intelligence and 3D laser scanning for MEP applications
summary: This article explores how artificial intelligence (AI) and 3D laser scanning can significantly benefit Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) applications. It highlights how 3D laser scanning provides crucial accurate data for new construction or retrofitting projects, while AI can then process this data for pattern recognition, identifying optimal and energy-efficient solutions, and enhancing project management. The combination of these technologies, along with human expertise, is presented as a powerful tool for improving efficiency and decision-making in MEP design and implementation.

title: SANUS Launches Speaker Stands and Wall Mounts for the New Sonos® Era 100™ and Era 300™ Wireless Speakers
summary: SANUS has launched a new line of height-adjustable and fixed-height speaker stands and wall mounts specifically designed for the new Sonos Era 100 and Era 300 wireless speakers. These accessories are available in black or white and are engineered for easy installation while preserving Sonos' premium sound quality and complementing their design. The stands are available now, with wall mounts launching in Q2 2023.

title: STMicroelectronics provides full STM32 support for Microsoft Visual Studio Code
summary: STMicroelectronics has announced full support for its STM32 microcontrollers within Microsoft Visual Studio Code (VS Code), a popular Integrated Development Environment (IDE). This integration allows developers to design, code, and debug STM32 applications directly in VS Code, leveraging features like IntelliSense and making the STM32 ecosystem more accessible to a broader range of developers. The move aims to connect high-level software developers, academics, and enthusiasts with the power of the STM32 family of microcontrollers, expanding its reach significantly.

title: 7 Cloud Computing Stocks That Can Make You a Millionaire as Data Explodes
summary: The article highlights seven cloud computing stocks—Salesforce, Microsoft, Snowflake, Amazon, IBM, Veeva Systems, and Alphabet—that are poised for growth as the demand for data storage and processing continues to explode. Despite a challenging 2022 for tech stocks, the public cloud sector demonstrated significant growth, indicating a strong migration of data to the cloud. Each company is detailed with its market position, recent financial performance, and reasons for its potential as a millionaire-maker investment.

title: Using the power of Cloudflare’s global network to detect malicious domains using machine learning
summary: Cloudflare leverages its global network and machine learning to detect malicious domains, focusing on two key threat techniques: Domain Generation Algorithms (DGAs) and DNS tunneling. The company uses advanced neural networks, including transformer-based models and gradient-boosted decision trees, to classify and identify these threats. Their system processes all DNS queries through the 1.1.1.1 resolver to swiftly identify and mitigate these evolving cyber threats.

title: 무위험지표금리 ETF 인기에 미국판 출격 대기
summary: 한국의 무위험지표금리(KOFR) 추종 ETF가 큰 인기를 얻자, 국내 자산운용사 4곳이 미국의 무위험지표금리(SOFR)를 추종하는 ETF 상장을 준비 중이다. 이 SOFR ETF는 달러를 보유한 기관 및 개인 투자자들이 은행 파킹통장처럼 활용할 수 있으며, 이르면 다음 달 삼성자산운용이 첫 상품을 출시할 예정이다. 투자자들은 KOFR ETF의 성공에 이어 SOFR ETF도 안정적인 달러 운용처로서 주목할 것으로 예상된다.

title: Morgan Stanley partners with OpenAI on internal chatbot for its advisors
summary: Morgan Stanley is partnering with OpenAI to create an internal-facing chatbot for its financial advisors, leveraging OpenAI's latest GPT-4 technology. This chatbot will provide advisors with instant, accurate answers generated exclusively from Morgan Stanley's proprietary content library, aiming to enhance efficiency and client service. This initiative is part of the firm's broader exploration into AI-powered tools, though Morgan Stanley emphasizes that human advice and advisor-client relationships will remain central to its wealth management strategy.

title: SAP Introduces SAP Datasphere to Simplify Customers’ Data Landscape
summary: SAP announced SAP Datasphere, the next generation of its data management portfolio, designed to simplify customers’ data landscapes and provide easy access to business-ready data. The company also unveiled strategic partnerships with Confluent, Databricks, Collibra, and DataRobot to enrich SAP Datasphere, enabling organizations to create unified architectures combining SAP and non-SAP data. This initiative aims to eliminate the complexity and "hidden data tax" associated with integrating disparate data sources, empowering customers with faster insights and improved decision-making.

title: Demo of China’s Answer to ChatGPT Disappoints Investors
summary: Baidu Inc.'s CEO Robin Li unveiled "Ernie Bot," China's answer to ChatGPT, in a recorded video demonstration that disappointed investors, leading to a 6.4% drop in Baidu's shares. The pre-recorded nature of the demo and lack of real-time interaction raised questions about Ernie's capabilities compared to OpenAI's ChatGPT. Despite the initial disappointment, Baidu is considered a frontrunner in China's AI race, planning to integrate Ernie Bot across its services while navigating concerns about US tech restrictions and Chinese regulatory oversight.

title: China’s Answer to ChatGPT Gets an Artificial Debut and Disappoints (Published 2023)
summary: Baidu's debut of its ChatGPT rival, Ernie, disappointed investors after its "live" demonstration was revealed to be prerecorded, causing Baidu's shares to tumble. This event highlights China's ongoing efforts to catch up with the United States in AI development, particularly given restrictions on high-end computing chips. The botched rollout also points to the intensive global race in large language model technology, dominated by a few major players.

title: Lumen’s Exec Team Taking The Provider From ‘Channel-Friendly’ To ‘Channel-Focused’
summary: Lumen Technologies is transitioning from a "channel-friendly" to a "channel-focused" organization, driven by a new C-suite with strong channel backgrounds. This shift involves significant internal investments in strategic services and a greater emphasis on customer experience, with partners playing a crucial role. The company's leadership is actively engaging with partners and expanding its partner programs to foster growth and improve collaboration.

title: NICE Achieves Milestone of One Million Agents on CXone
summary: NICE has reached a significant milestone with one million agents and supervisors now using its CXone cloud platform, following its recognition by Gartner and integration of OpenAI's generative modeling. The company reported strong financial results for 2022, including a 10% increase in total revenue and 26% growth in cloud revenue, securing several eight-figure deals. NICE projects continued growth for 2023, leveraging its strong market position, cloud expansion, and AI advancements.

title: Global Corporations Join Brookfield to Invest Nearly a Billion Dollars in Closed Loop Partners' Operating Company, Circular Services, the Leading Developer of Circular Economy Infrastructure
summary: Closed Loop Partners announced that six major corporations – Microsoft, Nestlé, PepsiCo, SK Group, Starbucks, and Unilever – are joining Brookfield to invest nearly a billion dollars in Circular Services. This investment aims to scale circular economy infrastructure and services in the United States, focusing on packaging, organics, textiles, and electronics. Circular Services, already the largest privately held recycling company in the U.S., will use these funds to upgrade recycling capabilities and prevent billions in landfill disposal costs, fostering a transition to a circular economy.

title: Los avisos de consumo que implementó el BBVA en la app (incluye débito)
summary: BBVA has implemented an immediate consumption alert system in its banking app, including for debit card transactions, which was not previously available through traditional card services like Visa Home or MasterConsultas. This new feature provides real-time notifications for purchases, improving security and enabling better tracking of expenses, especially for travelers. The author discusses the system's effectiveness, contrasting it with the outdated notifications from card networks, and hopes other banks will adopt similar immediate alert systems.

title: The 3 Best Cloud Computing ETFs to Buy for Long-Term Growth
summary: This article recommends three cloud computing ETFs for long-term growth, citing McKinsey's prediction of a $3 trillion EBITDA increase by 2030 from cloud adoption. It details the First Trust Cloud Computing ETF (SKYY), WisdomTree Cloud Computing Fund (WCLD), and ARK Next Generation Internet ETF (ARKW), highlighting their management styles, holdings, and performance. The author emphasizes diversification over single-company bets like Microsoft for cloud investing.

title: AB US Low Volatility Equity ETF Holdings
summary: This article details the holdings of the AB US Low Volatility Equity ETF (LOWV), which was established on March 22, 2023. The ETF focuses on large- and mid-cap US stocks, actively managed to achieve lower volatility than the broader market. Key holdings include major technology companies like Alphabet, Microsoft, Apple, NVIDIA, and Amazon, alongside diversified investments across various sectors.

title: Lumen CEO Kate Johnson is drawing on her experience at Microsoft to turn around a $19 billion business
summary: Kate Johnson, formerly president of Microsoft U.S., became CEO of Lumen Technologies in November, taking on the challenge of transforming the $19.6 billion-in-revenue enterprise telecom and networking company. Drawing on her experiences at Microsoft and other tech giants, Johnson aims to simplify the organization, foster innovation, and enhance customer focus, calling 2023 a "reset year." While her financial remit at Lumen is smaller than at Microsoft, she is now leading a complete company overhaul, transitioning it into the digital era while continuing daily operations.

title: AB US High Dividend ETF Holdings
summary: The AB US High Dividend ETF (HIDV) was established on March 22, 2023, by AB Funds, focusing its investment portfolio on high dividend yield equities. The actively managed fund, with $204.31 million in assets under management and 109 holdings, selects large- and mid-cap US stocks using a proprietary systemic approach. Key holdings include NVIDIA Corp, Apple Inc, Microsoft Corp, Broadcom Inc, and Alphabet Inc.

title: Microsoft recognized as a Leader in The Forrester Wave™: Data Security Platforms, Q1 2023
summary: Microsoft has been recognized as a Leader in The Forrester Wave™: Data Security Platforms, Q1 2023 report, highlighting its strong capabilities in data classification, threat visibility, and privacy solutions. The company's comprehensive Microsoft Purview suite and integrated ecosystem are lauded for their ability to help organizations protect sensitive data and mitigate risks. This recognition underscores Microsoft's significant investments in data security, reinforced by positive feedback from customers.

title: Digital Economy Discovers a Potential Frontier for Growth Thanks to Generative AI
summary: Generative AI, exemplified by large language models like GPT-3, is revolutionizing artificial intelligence, offering significant leaps in capabilities, speed, and cost-effectiveness. This new wave of AI is poised to drive massive innovation, boosting productivity and creating new applications across various sectors. The article explores how this technology will particularly impact and create opportunities in cloud computing, cybersecurity, and digital media, leading to substantial investment and growth in these areas.

title: Procter & Gamble confirm breach
summary: Procter & Gamble confirmed that one of its companies was affected by the Fortra GoAnywhere vulnerability, leading to a breach where attackers obtained some employee information. The company stated that no sensitive data like social security numbers, credit card details, or customer data was compromised, and business operations continue normally. The Russia-linked Cl0p ransomware syndicate, which claimed responsibility, has victimized numerous organizations using this zero-day flaw.

title: Microsoft Israel to lay off dozens as part of global cutbacks
summary: Microsoft Israel is preparing to lay off dozens of employees, impacting its cyber team for the first time, as part of Microsoft's broader global restructuring which includes 10,000 job cuts announced in January. The Israeli R&D center, employing about 2,700 people with half in cybersecurity, will see these layoffs primarily affect its security organization, with an estimated 10% reduction. This move follows other recent high-tech layoffs in Israel.

title: Cryptocurrencies add nothing useful to society, says chip-maker Nvidia
summary: Nvidia's chief technology officer, Michael Kagan, stated that cryptocurrencies bring nothing useful to society, despite the high demand for Nvidia's processors for crypto mining. He contrasted this with the value of AI applications like ChatGPT, which he believes represent a more worthwhile use of processing power. Nvidia had previously taken steps to limit the use of its graphics cards for crypto mining to prioritize supply for AI researchers and gamers.

title: Zoom jumps on ChatGPT bandwagon, integrates generative AI features
summary: Zoom is incorporating OpenAI's generative AI, the technology behind ChatGPT and GPT-4, into its video communications platform. These new features will generate Zoom Team Chat and email responses, and an AI feature for Zoom IQ will create shareable meeting summaries and whiteboard presentations. While initial availability is limited to select customers and specific products, Zoom plans a broader release, aiming to bolster its enterprise customer base through AI and automation.

title: Do AI-powered ETFs outperform their human-managed rivals?
